summary: Listed among the Maraketh's notable members (the list gives the name without a Sekhema title); one of the three akhara named on the Brutal Restraint Timeless Jewel. The corpus holds only list-level mentions, so details are limited.

sources.locator: Notable members list: '* [[Nasima]]' under the Maraketh section
Variant table: 'Nasima' with 'Denoted service of # dekhara in the akhara of Nasima'

name: Navali, Speaker of Hinekora
summary: Karui seer who guides the Exile through the Halls of the Dead and presents them to the Mother of Death. Also appeared in PoE1 (Prophecy, Ancestor).

alt_summaries.summary: NPC seer of Prophecy league who sells prophecies for silver coins.

name: The Neglected Flame
summary: Memory boss guarding the thread that leads to the Incarnation of Neglect; Eagon siphons its kernel.

name: Nenet
summary: Faridun rogue (the Scout) hireable for Perception jobs. Unlocked by a Tullina contract. Her questline was never released in-game: it would have had the exile seek the Book of Jamanra to prove the Jamanra existed.

sources.locator: Lead; "To unlock Nenet, run a contract with Tullina"; questline note
'Jamanra' section: 'Nenet, a Faridun, tasked the exile with finding the Book of Jamanra'

name: Nessa
summary: Healer and vendor at Lioneye's Watch, taught Brutus's tale in Theopolis schools; gives Mercy Mission, Siren's Cadence.

sources.locator: NPCs; Mercy Mission, Caged Brute dialogue

alt_summaries.summary: Oriathan refugee at Lioneye's Watch transformed by the Brine King into a mermaid bride.

name: Niko the Mad
summary: Master-NPC miner who guides the Exile into the Azurite Mine; collects Voltaxic Sulphite to power his Crawler (a repurposed Eternal torture device) and generator.

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4 master who introduces Delve content in Highgate.

name: Niles
summary: Former Templar interrogator, hireable rogue in the Rogue Harbour (Counter-thaumaturgy). Unlocked by a Huck contract; his contract unlocks Vinderi.

sources.locator: Lead and Lore: "He is the former interrogator of the Templar"; "To unlock Niles, run a contract with Huck")

name: Oak
summary: Bandit lord of the Wetlands; preaches peace ('To spare the lives of many, you need take only one'), fights Alira's thralls; wears Oak's Amulet, one of three pieces of the Apex.

name: Olroth
summary: Leader of the Knights of the Sun, called the Gallant and later the Grim. Recorded the Empty-Eyed Fiend's killing of a young woman, fought the Fiend with a gem, was stabbed by priests, and returned as the undying horror the exile fights as the Expedition league boss.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)
Olroth, Origin of the Fall: excavate a Kalguuran Tomb in an Expedition Logbook at area level 79+

alt_summaries.summary: Knights of the Sun leader, 'the Gallant' then 'the Grim'; staked the Triskelion Flame, defeated the Empty-Eyed Fiend with a gem, was stabbed by priests; now boss Olroth, Origin of the Fall.

Leader of the Knights of the Sun (Origin of the Fall / the Gallant / the Grim); stole the Triskelion Flame, doomed the expedition and villages, and was found by Dannig and the Exile sustained by it. Motive unknown.

Expedition faction leader sought in the last stage of The Grand Expedition; a Kalguuran Tomb excavation at area level 79+ opens the pinnacle 'Olroth, Origin of the Fall' (guide). Guide claims he leads the Knights of the Sun and guards the Triskelion Flame (low).

name: Lord Mayor Ondar
summary: Mayor of Sarn who, with gems implanted for the occasion, betrayed and killed Emperor Chitus during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons celebration, during the Purity Rebellion (1334 IC).

sources.locator: section 'Assassination of Chitus' and 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

alt_summaries.summary: Sarn's Lord Mayor, betrayed and killed Chitus with a Black Elixir weapon, then was cut down by Chitus.

name: Orbala
summary: Maraketh warrior, known as the Sekhema of Sekhemas, who fought the 'bandit king of Stridevolf'; PoE2 shows she was the mortal identity of Garukhan before her ascension. That she was also the traveller who freed Sin from Innocence's worshippers is only suggested by relic lore (inferred).

sources.locator: Lore: former human Sekhema Orbala (revealed in PoE2)

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh warrior who fought the 'bandit king of Stridevolf'; PoE2 states she was the mortal identity of Garukhan before ascension, known as the Sekhema of Sekhemas. PoE1 3.22 relics (a traveller freeing Sin from Innocence's worshippers) are suggested, not confirmed, to be her.

name: Oshabi, Avatar of the Grove
summary: Boss form of Oshabi. It is triggered in a Map Device by a Sacred Blossom map fragment; the Heart of the Grove, grown from a harvested Tier 4 seed, is the separate challenge that leads to the Avatar of the Grove.

sources.locator: lead; Dialogue: Introduction, The Grove, Lifeforce, Exile from the Azmeri
League mechanic: Heart of the Grove

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri outcast, exiled by her tribe after she offered a child to the earth when she alone still heard the land's whispers. Tends the Sacred Grove, names the energy Lifeforce and asks the exile to harvest seeds. After the tutorial quest she turns into the Heart of the Grove; she returns as Oshabi, Avatar of the Grove, a boss.

name: Overseer Krow
summary: Slave Pens overseer boss blocking access to Overseer's Tower.

name: Oyun
summary: Maraketh akhara leader at Highgate; recounts Deshret's sealing of the Beast.

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh Sekhema (ruler) of Highgate kidnapped by Kira to be sacrificed to Garukhan; the exile fails to save her.

name: Petarus and Vanja
summary: Relic-hunter duo of Highgate who seek Garukhan's Storm Blade and bottle its storm.

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4 jewellery, flask and gem vendors in Highgate.

name: Piety of Theopolis
summary: Former Vinia of Oriath, pardoned by Dominus; thaumaturge making miscreations in Sarn; saved by Malachai; becomes an Abomination in Act 4; eventually killed by Malachai.

sources.locator: Lore: Background and In Path of Exile
Lore: Background and In Path of Exile

name: Putembo
summary: Tyrant of the primeval civilisation who forced subjects to quarry stone for his fortress; overthrown by Aul.

name: Qianga
summary: Named on a Gilded Shaper Scarab as the 'Deliverer of the Sealing Blade to the Watchers'; probably an Order of the Djinn member (wiki says unclear).

name: Quilon Bardiya
summary: Founder of House Bardiya, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

name: Rakiata
summary: Chieftain of the Tasalio tribe; after her father the chieftain was felled by invaders she took up arms, entrusted a fragment of a fabled spear to the sea, and fights in a dance-like style emulating Tasalio's tide; Ikiaho vouched for her in the Halls.

chronology.relative: deceased Karui chieftain, resides in the Halls of the Dead

name: Ratha Azadi
summary: Founder of House Azadi, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

name: Raulf, the Recruiter
summary: Meridian Free Traders agent who recruits labourers and specialists for Kingsmarch; refuses to be anyone's spy.

name: Raulo (Fidelitas)
summary: Maligaro's slave and lover, injected with Calibric Extantia and renamed Fidelitas.

name: Ridan, Afarud Commander
summary: Afarud boss in mirages; drops The Black Barya.

name: Rigwald, the Wolven King
summary: Ezomyte thane of Ezomyr who received Victario's letters seeking aid for the Purity Rebellion; possessed by the Greatwolf during the Rebellion. Boss of the Talisman league; his memoirs are the Inscription lore found at Stone Altars. NOT a member of the Immortal Syndicate (the Betrayal video only notes Thane Jorgin shares the title 'thane' with him).

sources.locator: Rigwald, the Wolven King: boss of the Talisman league
The Greatwolf: Rigwald possessed during the Purity Rebellion
Victario wrote letters to Thane Rigwald of Ezomyr

alt_summaries.summary: Ezomyte thane who killed King Skothe and led the Bloody Flowers Rebellion.

name: Riker Maloney
summary: Syndicate member without established background. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Rin Yuushu
summary: Syndicate member from the Mutewind warband. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Rog, the Disenchanter
summary: Kalguuran dealer who runs the Kingsmarch disenchanting apothecary and dreams of his own shop; manages the group's tabletop game; former rebel.

sources.locator: Rog searches for his missing wife, Gwennen

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran dealer and Expedition NPC who sells identified rare equipment and takes Order artifacts; he manages the tabletop-style game the Kalguuran NPCs play.
Kalguuran trader, Alva's contact in Kingsmarch, who sells the Boat Charter; returning from PoE1's Settlers of Kalguur.
Kalguuran trader at Kingsmarch who arranged the charter in Act 4; searches for his wife Gwennen in 0.5.

name: Romira Phrecian
summary: Emperor who fed his wife's sons (fathered by his brother) back to her; deposed in the Night of a Thousand Ribbons.

name: Cardinal Sanctus Vox
summary: Oriathan noble, ancestor of the Vox family; general of the Templar legion.

name: Saresh
aliases: Saresh, Necromancer of the Weeping Black
summary: Faridun reject and necromancer of Weeping Black, former Order of the Djinn member; defeated by Garukhan (Orbala) with the Horn of the Vastiri.

sources.locator: Vanja: 'ancient battle against the necromancer Saresh'

alt_summaries.summary: Historical Faridun necromancer and Order of the Djinn member slain by Garukhan; endgame boss in The Black Barya.
Historical Faridun reject and Order of the Djinn member who explored intrinsic darkness and raised undead until killed by Garukhan; his name is on Metamorph Scarabs.

Necromancer (with an undead horde) whom Garukhan fought in the eastern desert, when she lost the Storm Blade - according to the relic hunters Petarus and Vanja's research; nothing else is said about him, and his date is unknown.

name: Sasan, the Bandit Lord
summary: Bandit Lord who takes Atlas Runners hostage while they map; defeat him or pay 50,000 Gold; drops The Living Blade and The Bandit Lord's Band.

name: The Shaper
summary: Valdo Caeserius reduced by the Elder's memory-feeding to a shell who 'shapes' worlds in the Atlas and no longer recognises Zana. Guarded by four Guardians of the Void; pinnacle boss in the Shaper's Realm.

sources.locator: Memory of Awakening: 'I will forge a world anew'
Zana: 'the Shaper was in reality Zana's father, Valdo'

name: Shavronne of Umbra
summary: One of Malachai's 'Godless Three'; her returned spirit is killed in Shavronne's Tower so Sin can harvest her soul.

alt_summaries.summary: Vain thaumaturge of the Godless Three who experimented on Brutus at Axiom Prison.
Thaumaturge of the Godless Three who created Brutus; Act 4 boss guarding Malachai's heart.

name: Silk
summary: Storyteller/artist of the Forest Encampment (Sin notes many Azmeri-descended artists worship Arakaali) who falls for Arakaali in Act 7, calls her his bride and is lost when the exile kills her. Earlier he asks the exile for Black Venom from Maligaro's pet spider (Web of Secrets).

sources.locator: Silk asks for venom from Black Death, Maligaro's pet spider

alt_summaries.summary: Forest Encampment hero-storyteller who lost his spear in the Weaver's eye; shares word of the stone seal near Prisoner's Gate.

name: Siosa
summary: Ghost in the Library, friend of Icius Perandus, gem vendor after A Fixture of Fate.

name: Sirus, Awakener of Worlds
summary: Smuggler and leader of the Elderslayers who loved Zana; sacrificed himself into the Arcana trap and returned empty and mad. He burned Oriath and is a pinnacle boss; journals narrate his fall.

name: Sister Cassia
summary: Former Templar-circle mechanical artisan and Blight NPC who runs the Purification Pump encounters and the Anoint bench; exiled by High Templar Dominus for subverting his virtue-gem projects, and replaced by Piety. Believes Blighted maps lead to the Blight's source.

sources.locator: lead; Dialogue: Exile, Replacement, Devices, Fungi, Blighted Maps

name: Solerai
summary: Legendary Maraketh Sekhema who with Lundara ended the Winter of the World; possibly Solaris.

name: Sonja, the Farmer
summary: Kingsmarch farmer puzzled by the thriving plants on supposedly barren soil.

name: Sumei
summary: Historical Maraketh Order of the Djinn 'Master Lorekeeper' who investigated artefact duplication caused by Kalandra's influence.

name: Tacati, Architect of Toxins
summary: Unique Architect found in the Poison Garden, Cultivar Chamber and Toxic Grove rooms of the Temple of Atzoatl; his name gives the legacy Tacati item mods.

name: Tane Octavius
summary: Freed slave and alchemist exiled for killing his abusive master Lucan Octavius; works from an underground laboratory (Karui Shores) to isolate 'intrinsic darkness' from the flesh of monsters via Metamorphs, hoping to purify a cruel soul.

sources.locator: lead; Dialogue: Tane's Master, Exile, Vision, Goals

name: Tangmazu, the Raven Trickster
summary: Trickster god, brother of Ralakesh, who tricked Solaris into believing Lunaris had betrayed her (PoE1 lore: Strange Voice in Delirium). In PoE2 0.5 he is the Raven Trickster whose defeat completes Strange Reflection and the Delirium storyline.

sources.locator: Tangmazu: trickster god, Ralakesh's brother, Delirium NPC, also Tekaru / the Black Crow

name: Tarcus Veruso
summary: Azmeri leader and first Emperor (Prima Imperialus) who led 80,000 Azmeri to found Sarn in 1 IC. A ruthless despot, he outlawed thaumaturgy, buried the gems under Highgate, and created the legion system.

name: Tarkleigh
summary: Veteran exile and smuggler at Lioneye's Watch; weapon and armour vendor who gives out quests and skill gems; mentions Dominus took the exiles' history.

sources.locator: Enemy at the Gate quest dialogue
Enemy at the Gate quest dialogue

alt_summaries.summary: Lioneye's Watch veteran who vendors and gives quests in Act 6, and mourns Nessa.

name: Tasuni
summary: Maraketh seer at Highgate who hears Deshret's spirit.

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh man of Highgate, brother of Kira, who contends with Irasha for rule of Highgate; he asks the exile to put his sister down, recover the Sekhema Feather and, if possible, return Oyun.

name: Tawhanuku
summary: Chieftain of the Hinekora tribe in the Karui Ancestor roster.

chronology.relative: deceased Karui chieftain, resides in the Halls of the Dead

name: Tecrod
summary: 'The Hated Slave': Abyssal Lich Lord who, unlike Amanamu, Kurgal and Ulaman, acts independently of Kulemak (PoE1 wiki: forsaken by Kulemak for unclear reasons). In PoE2 (Legacy of the Precursors) he steals the Flame Seed on his wyrm, seeks Kulemak's favour, hunts for the Edicts and is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity.

sources.locator: Lore: independent of Kulemak; steals Flame Seed; destroyed by Arbiter of Divinity
Lich Lords: Tecrod, the disgraced Abyssal Lich, forsaken by Kulemak; freed from a Precursor sarcophagus, seeks to win back Kulemak favour

alt_summaries.summary: White-haloed Abyssal Lich Lord ('the Hated Slave'). The PoE2 wiki says that, unlike Amanamu, Kurgal and Ulaman, he acts independently of Kulemak's other lords and is active in the Epilogue hunting the Edicts; the PoE wiki adds he was forsaken by Kulemak, is freed from a Precursor sarcophagus and seeks to win back Kulemak's favour. He steals the Flame Seed, incapacitates the Exile at the Origin Tower claiming the First Edict's power for 'the Master' (probably Kulemak, inferred), and is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity.

Abyssal Lich Lord ('the Hated Slave') with a white halo; unlike Amanamu, Kurgal and Ulaman he acts independently of Kulemak and hunts the Edicts. Appears as a wyrm rider who steals the Flame Seed after the Arbiter of Ash falls; when the Exile places the Origin Core in the Origin Tower his wyrm incapacitates the Exile and he claims the power for 'the Master', but the Arbiter of Divinity destroys his body.

name: Queen Tetzlapokal
summary: Pre-Atziri Vaal queen, devotee of Arakaali with a fascination with death and corpses; the Vaal City rose to prominence in her reign.

name: Thane Jorgin
summary: Syndicate member (Betrayal, 3.5.0) who left as a mere after being accused of killing his brother; believes Rin or another Brotherhood of Silence member responsible (per video). Video notes he shares the title 'thane' with Rigwald; Jun mocks his 'first ones' (Ezomyte) background.

name: The Black Knight
summary: Boss guarding Verisium Outcrops in the Starfall Crater (reached via map ore deposits); drops Svalinn.

name: The Boss of the Ring
summary: The unnamed 'Boss' who leads the Ring, per Kurai's dialogue ('the Boss has no tolerance for guests who do not obey his rules'). Identity is not established in the wiki; any name is fan theory.

sources.locator: 'The Ring' dialogue: 'The Boss would like to offer you the opportunity'

name: The Dreamer
summary: Keepers-league NPC (full name: Chayula, the Benevolent Dreamer / the One Who Dreamt) found hidden in the Monastery of the Keepers. After the failed fusion of the five Breachlords he was torn asunder and cast into the void; he gave Ailith visions and the Genesis Tree as weapon against the Hiveborn, calls the Exile an ally 'for now', and destroys Ailith's body when she learns the truth (she is a preserved Hiveborn copy).

sources.locator: Dialogue ("Who are you?", "Who is our enemy?", Enter Back Room) and Lore
Visions V: the Four have become One; Genesis Tree is his gift
Lore: Chayula spoke to humans through dreams, founding the Keepers

name: The Hooded One
summary: Unnamed Hooded One bound by a runed sword in the Grelwood's Tree of Souls, later revealed as Sin (Thief of Virtue) who created the Beast; guides the Exile through Acts 1-3.

sources.locator: Quest log 'Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine to the Northwest'
Quote 'I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin.'
Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine: 'I am... a god. I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin.'

alt_summaries.summary: Dark hooded god-like figure, likely Sin (PoE2 wiki inference), impaled by Count Geonor who takes the Seed of Corruption from him in PoE2's opening cinematic; in the endgame quest Legacy of the Precursors he sleeps in thrall to the Beast's corruption and is the intended wielder of the Precursor Weapon. A YouTube lore creator says Act 4 hints he was once a Precursor (community theory, unconfirmed).

The god Sin in disguise (identity confessed in Act 2: 'I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin'). In Act 4 he reforges the Weapon, recognises Precursor writing from a faded mortal childhood, cures Tavakai and organises the alliance; in the endgame he sleeps under the Beast's Corruption.

Mysterious guide of the PoE2 Exile, revealed in Act 2 to be the god Sin, the Thief of Virtue and creator of the Beast. Recognises Precursor writing from a mortal childhood memory, forges the Weapon, and in the Epilogue lies in corruption-induced sleep.
Guide figure in PoE2 who directs the Exile to the Vaal and the weapon.

name: The King in the Mists
summary: Chief of the Nameless shadow creatures in the Viridian Wildwood and enemy of the Maji. Boss of Affliction (PoE1, 3.23) and, in PoE2 Act 1 (Freythorn), the cult 'king' guarding the final Ritual altar. In Legacy of the Maji, Aoife recalls being drawn to him, believing him one of the Maji of old.

sources.locator: unique items 'the King in the Mists'
'The King in the Mists encounter added to Ritual'
Unique items: drops from the King in the Mists
Aoife dialogue about the King in the Mists
Aoife: 'You killed him in your domain... but now he returns from his'; step 17 Defeat the King in the Mists; step 20 Pick up the Head of the King
Killing the King drops The Head of the King, which starts the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth

alt_summaries.summary: Major antagonist of Affliction league, a shadowy Nameless force within the Viridian Wildwood against whom the Maji wage a long war; later added to Ritual in 3.25.

Boss who killed Aoife and whose effigies tether him to the world; killed once in the campaign (Ogham) yet returns in the endgame Ritual quest, where he is fought at the Crux of Nothingness; his Head starts the Rite of the Nameless. Drawing power from the Bodach is a guide claim.

name: The Last to Die
summary: Last of the Vaal High Priest bloodline bound by Chaos's pact to the Blood Crucible; appears from the Coast in Scourge, asking the exile to continue in her place; Kalandra says she 'wanders still, forever fleeing, forever burdened by guilt'.

name: The Shade
summary: Name Valdo gave the Elder's free-roaming spirit in his dreams; it taught him thaumaturgy and said the Map Device would link the dreamlands to Wraeclast, then asked him to pull the sword (Starforge) from its body.

name: The Trialmaster
summary: Servant of Chaos who runs the Trials of Chaos. Introduced in PoE1's Ultimatum league and encountered in PoE2 Act 3 and the endgame Trialmaster arena.

chronology.relative: Captured in the Vaal era; active in PoE1 3.14+ and PoE2 Act 3

sources.locator: Lead: "the Trialmaster offers the Trials of Chaos"
Lead: "He will offer the Trials of Chaos ... as directed by his master, Chaos"
Lead: Chaos is the Trialmaster's master
Ixchel entry: captured infiltrating the Temple of Chaos, became the Trialmaster

alt_summaries.summary: Minimal node (owned by PoE2 domain): per the Order of the Djinn page, the Trialmaster is the former Order member Ixchel, 'Godstealer'.
The servant of Chaos who oversees the Trials of Chaos and tests challengers for Chaos's amusement. At least several thousand years old.
Servant of Chaos who runs the Trial: 'My master, Chaos, has charged me with this task.'

name: The Weaver
summary: Giant spider ('mother of all eight-legs') in the Weaver's Chambers, in whose eye Silk's spear (Maligaro's Spike) is lodged; killed by the Exile.

name: Tibbs
summary: Brute-force and demolition rogue hireable in the Rogue Harbour. Running a contract with him unlocks Tullina.

sources.locator: Lead; "To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs" (Tullina page)
Lead: "To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs, the Giant"

name: Tolman
summary: Clarissa's lover, captured with her in the Slums and tortured to death by Piety of Theopolis in the Crematorium (Act 3); in Act 8 his zombie returns, and the failed resurrection at the Quay forces the exile to kill him.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: Tolman attacks after the ritual fails

alt_summaries.summary: Clarissa's boyfriend, tortured to death by Piety in the Crematorium; reappears as a zombie in Act 8.

name: Tora, Master of the Hunt
summary: Forsaken master (ranged weapons); studied corruption in beasts. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Tujen, the Haggler / Harbourmaster
summary: Kalguuran haggler turned Kingsmarch harbourmaster who crews ships; former rebel who lost friends (Tolis, Oskar, Naja, Thea, Sven) and vows revenge; in PoE2 asks the Exile to clear the fog at Kedge Bay.

sources.locator: Tujen: 'Kingsmarch trade has seen better days'

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran haggler and Expedition NPC who sells non-equipment items and takes Black Scythe artifacts; Harbourmaster of Kingsmarch.
Kalguuran haggler/harbourmaster of Kingsmarch; gives Dark Mists and recalls the town's founding.

name: Tullina
summary: Agility rogue (the Catburglar). Her heist target is Merveil's Wedding Dress, which the History page ties to the Oriath wedding of Daresso and Merveil. Unlocked by a Tibbs contract; her contract unlocks Nenet.

sources.locator: Lead: "To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs, the Giant"
'Daresso and Merveil' section: Merveil's wedding dress as a Heist target

name: Tyndarus Phrecius
summary: Emperor c. 870-892 IC, backed by High Templar Andronicus; lost the Trarthan war of independence.

alt_summaries.summary: Eternal Empire emperor who in 870 IC sent Phrecian legions to Trarthus to suppress the warlords' rebellion and capitulated after two years.

name: Uhtred
summary: High Priest of the Order of the Chalice who declared the Vaal gems unclean, admitted responsibility for the attack on Olroth, and fled to an ancient shrine. Returns as the PoE1 boss Uhtred, Covetous Traitor.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran expedition member who declared virtue gems unclean and succumbed to corruption-driven madness before discovering a dark mirror.
High Priest of the Order of the Chalice who disliked gems, plotted against Olroth and fled to the Precursor Shrine; now Uhtred, Covetous Traitor.
Expedition faction leader, 'Uhtred, the Stardrinker', fought in a tomb in The Grand Expedition; link to the Verisium meteor is suggested only by the 'Stardrinker' title and guides (low).

name: Ulaman, Sovereign of the Well
summary: Abyssal Lich, commander of the Lightless and servant of Kulemak. Boss of the Abyssal Depths (Abyss league 3.1.0).

alt_summaries.summary: Ulaman is an Abyssal Lich and one of Kulemak's three most powerful servants commanding the Lightless.
Lich Lord under Kulemak; Abyssal Depths boss.

name: Undertaker Arimor
summary: Undertaker who gathers the haunted dead of Wraeclast, gives the Exile the Lantern of Arimor and runs the Necropolis; invokes a god named Thruldana during his chants.

sources.locator: ===Thruldana=== "A god whose name is invoked by Undertaker Arimor during one of his chants."

name: Utula
summary: Karui slave-rebellion leader and high priest of Kitava in Oriath; has Casticus's eyes taken to enter the Templar Courts, then uses Innocence's fall to complete the King's Feast and summon Kitava; killed by the Exile.

alt_summaries.summary: Chieftain of the Kitava tribe; his text covers High Templar Avarius.

name: Uzaza, the First King
summary: Founder of the primeval civilisation who led his people on a migration in a cold winter; named on Uzaza's rings.

name: The Vaal Omnitect
summary: Vaal construct, boss of the present-day Temple of Atzoatl during the Incursion leagues; its exclusive currency drops come from it.

sources.locator: 'Currency' / 'Unique items': 'The Vaal Omnitect, the boss of The Temple of Atzoatl'

name: Vagan, Weaponmaster
summary: Duelist forsaken master (weapons). Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Valdo Caeserius
summary: Chief Arkhon of the Oriath academy and father of Zana; dreamed of the Elder's dreamlands, was pulled into the Atlas, and fought the Elder until it ate his memories, becoming the Shaper. Aberration quotes show him grieving his Templar-killed wife.

name: Valerie, the Corsair
summary: Pondium-born corsair captain who borrowed the Sovereign from its masked, Templar-linked builders and freed Vesper's soul; recruits Exiles as first mates.

sources.locator: Dialogue: The Forge, Pondium, The Sovereign

name: Varashta, the Winter Sekhema
summary: Former Maraketh Sekhema who projects herself near mirages and grants wishes; opposes Zarokh, the Grand Djinn of Time.

name: Velka, the Tide Witch
summary: Brinerot Shamanessa hunting the Allflame; boss in Kishara's Rest.

name: High Templar Venarius
summary: Puritanical High Templar who destroyed heretical texts and commissioned Valdo to assemble the Map Device; kidnapped Zana to force Valdo into the dreamlands, bargained with the Elder for power and was killed by it. In Synthesis he appears as a memory boss.

sources.locator: Valdo Caeserius: 'Venarius tried to negotiate with the Elder ... it killed Venarius and his men'

alt_summaries.summary: Historical High Templar who commissioned Valdo Caeserius to build a map device.

name: Veritania, the Redeemer
summary: Scholar elderslayer who retreats into puritan disgust at the Atlas' vices and becomes the Redeemer.

name: Veruso, Prima Imperialus
summary: Eternal Empire figure who placed the Ankh of Eternity in a Quay shrine at the dawn of the Empire; his wife Chiara was changed by it.

sources.locator: Clarissa: Veruso, Prima Imperialus, placed the Ankh; what it did to his wife Chiara

name: Vesper
summary: Valerie's childhood friend whose body lies aboard the Sovereign while his soul is bound to the ship; runs Allflame crafting.

name: Vic Vox
summary: Victario 'Vic' Vox, one of the two Vox twin bosses of the Heist unique contract 'Contract: The Twins'. Member of the Vox family, descendant of Cardinal Sanctus Vox, named after the poet Victario. After Kurai steals the book 'O' Eternal' for a client he declares war on her, kidnaps and kills her cat Hana, and is killed with his twin by Kurai and the Exile.

sources.locator: 'The Negotiation', 'Returned To Rogue Harbour' and 'The Twins' sections

name: Victario
summary: A Sarn poet and art critic who joined the Purity Rebellion, created the Ancient Graffiti in Sarn, and led the uprisings in the Slums and Docks. At the Night of a Thousand Ribbons ambush he shouted 'Death to Sin!'. Central figure of the comic Path of Exile: Origins.

sources.locator: sections 'The Purity Rebellion', 'Battle at the Grain Gate', 'Assassination of Chitus'

alt_summaries.summary: Poet who stirred rebellion with graffiti and letters to Rigwald; died in the Cataclysm.

Sarn poet and key supporter of the Purity Rebellion who incited Sarn against Emperor Chitus and Malachai; wrote to Thane Rigwald seeking Ezomyte aid; killed in Sarn during the Cataclysm. Named on the Elegant Hubris timeless jewel; father of Hyrri Ngamaku's child per wiki.
Sarn poet of the Purity Rebellion; stole three platinum busts; killed in the Cataclysm (comic Origins).

name: Vilenta
summary: Traitor who let Kitava's cultists into the Overseer's Tower; later a monster killed in the Control Blocks.

alt_summaries.summary: Scholar in the Overseer's Tower who studies corruption with her Miasmeter.

name: Vinderi
summary: Demolition and trap-disarmament rogue (the Dismantler) whose unique ability duplicates Heist chest contents. Unlocked by a Niles contract; his contract unlocks Gianna.

sources.locator: Lead and Heist ability; "To unlock Vinderi, run a contract with Niles"

name: Vinny Vox
summary: Vincent 'Vinny' Vox, twin brother of Vic Vox and co-boss of 'Contract: The Twins'. Descendant of Cardinal Sanctus Vox and member of the Vox family; the wiki states the Exile and Kurai kill both twins in the final contract.

name: Viper Napuatzi
summary: Vaal general of Utzaal's past who captures Alva and sends her to Doryani; defeated in the Utzaal time-gate sequence.

alt_summaries.summary: General of the Vaal legion in the Timeless Conflict. (General of the Vaal legion in Legion league, 3.7.0.)

Vaal warrior in Utzaal's past who confronts the Exile and Alva after the gate opens, accuses them of spilling Vaal blood, and has Alva taken to Doryani; defeated by the Exile in Act 3 (exact rank/title not given in the wiki quest log).

name: Volkuur, the Unbreathing Queen
summary: Boss of The Pale Court (Pale Council, Prophecy system); the wiki states the Pale Council fight no longer exists after 3.17.0. Drops Volkuur's Guidance.

sources.locator: Header: 'The prophecy system was removed from the game in version 3.17.0. The Pale Council fight no longer exists'; infobox location = The Pale Court; Drops: 'drops Volkuur's Guidance'

name: High Templar Voll
summary: High Templar who leads the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) against Chitus and becomes Emperor of the Eternal Empire. His reanimated remains in the Dried Lake are fought in Act 4.

sources.locator: section 'The Purity Rebellion' and 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: High Templar who led the Purity Rebellion, crowned Emperor 1334 IC, spared Malachai, and perished in the Cataclysm; undead at Dried Lake and defeated in Act 4.
High Templar Voll of Thebrus led the Purity Rebellion, became Emperor, spared Malachai, died in the Cataclysm; fought as the Brittle Emperor in the Dried Lake.

name: Vorana
summary: Black Scythe mercenary leader and Medved's beloved. She killed the twelve priests who stabbed Olroth, took gem-infused rites into her own flesh and left the walls. Returns as the boss Vorana, Last to Fall.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)
Medved, Vorana and Uhtred join Olroth as the 4 Faction Leaders

alt_summaries.summary: Black Scythes mercenary leader who took up gems and fought on; later Vorana, Last to Fall.
Leader of the Black Scythe mercenaries; used virtue gems against the nightbreeds and the Empty-Eyed Fiend, casting aside her primary virtue.
Expedition faction leader, 'Vorana, Last to Fall', fought in a tomb on the islands in The Grand Expedition.

name: Vorici, Master Assassin
summary: Forsaken master (socket/colour crafting); Brotherhood of Silence member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Vruun, Marshal of Xesht
summary: PoE2 boss in Unstable Breaches, marshal serving Xesht; drops Lineage supports.

sources.locator: Version History: introduced in 0.5.0; boss in Unstable Breaches

alt_summaries.summary: Breach marshal found in stabilised Unstable Breaches; Ailith's PoE1 Keepers quest asks the Exile to bring 'The Head of Vruun' and praises it as preparation for a second graft meld.
Breach boss in Unstable Breach encounters; drops the Head of Vruun used to grow the Grasping Orchid; introduced 0.5.0.

name: Weylam Roth
summary: Undead pirate captain of the Black Crest, grandfather of Lilly Roth. Summoned by burning the Black Flag at the Beacon, he is bound to ferry the exile to the Brine King's Reef and on to Phrecia (Act 7); he later appears at the Bridge Encampment and the Oriath docks (Act 10), where he asks for Atziri's Elixir of Allure.

sources.locator: Weylam asks for the Elixir of Allure in the Ossuary

name: Weylin
summary: Ezomyte slave poisoned by Chitus in the Labyrinth.

name: Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand
summary: Unique Breach monster (Atlas notable Call of Xesht-Ula, 3.17.0; no longer encounterable since 3.28.0) whose name is a portmanteau of the five Breachlords; summons apparitions of each lord and can drop any breachstone. The PoE2 wiki says the Breachlords had planned to merge into a being called Xesht-Ula. Not the same entity as Xesht.

sources.locator: Lore: Vaal Cult of the Purple Flame knew of the five Breachlords' plan to merge into Xesht-Ula

name: Xibaqua
summary: Mythic/historical figure of the Vaal Empire whose remains were believed to be the progenitor of all Vaal; Vaal myth says their conflict with 'the gods' produced a 'droplet of pure light', the first Vaal. Unclear whether myth or history.

alt_summaries.summary: Historical figure of the Vaal Empire whose remains were believed to be the original progenitor of all Vaal; born from flesh of ancient Vaal gods; named on a Glorious Vanity variant.

name: Xipocado, Royal Architect
summary: Atziri's Royal Architect who with Doryani rebuilt the temple as a self-modifying machine; boss in the Temple of Atzoatl (PoE1) and Atziri's Temple (PoE2).

alt_summaries.summary: Boss of Atziri's Temple; in PoE1 an enemy in past Temple of Atzoatl who built the Royal Meeting Room to Atziri's throne.

name: Yeena
summary: Dream-seer vendor in the Forest Encampment who dreams of the Great White Beast, the Golden Hand and the shadow climbing the Vaal pyramid.

sources.locator: Yeena dialogue; Shadow of the Vaal
Yeena dialogue; Shadow of the Vaal

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri survivor at the Bridge Encampment who brews Fire Dew to burn open Arakaali's temple.

name: Yriel, the Feral Lord
summary: Boss of The Pale Court or the 'The Feral Lord V' Prophecy encounter (Pale Council). Known for Blast Rain, Decoy Shot and beast-summoning traps; removed in 3.17.0 per the wiki.

sources.locator: Intro: 'a boss in The Pale Court or The Feral Lord V encounters'; Abilities list; Version history 3.17.0 'Removed from the game'

name: Zana, Master Cartographer
summary: Forsaken master (Master Cartographer) who survives Betrayal. The wiki has a separate page for Zana Caeserius 'the Originator' of Secrets of the Atlas; the Master page is linked as 'the former Master', implying the same person, but the identity is not spelled out here. Owned by another domain.

alt_summaries.summary: Master cartographer. In the older Epilogue Kirac blames 'Zana Caeserius' for the disappearance of his brother Baran, and in the Epilogue quest 'Brave New Worlds' (v3.1, since marked historical) Zana gives maps through portals; she belongs mainly to the Atlas/Master storylines of other domains.

Valdo's daughter. Orphaned, she fled Oriath before exile, found a Map Device in ruined Oriath and mapped the Atlas. She hunted the Shaper and Elder, hired the Elderslayers, sealed the device when they went mad and left the Atlas after Sirus burned Oriath.

name: Zana, the Originator
summary: Secrets of the Atlas NPC (also Zana Caeserius) who threads memories across the Atlas, working to destroy the Atlas, fracturing it into four quadrants. Nature uncertain: she declares 'I am not your sister' to Eagon, and her relation to the Zana of the Elderslayers era is not spelled out.

sources.locator: Witness Zana and Eagon: 'The only way is to destroy it ... The Atlas'

alt_summaries.summary: Zana Caeserius, the Originator, is trapped in the Atlas weaving memories to destroy it; tells Eagon 'I am not your sister' (ambiguous whether another Zana).

name: Zarokh, Grand Djinn of Time
summary: Djinn who siphons other djinn to project power; his mirage is bound by an Astral Chain.

sources.locator: Zarokh, the Temporal: complete all four Sekhemas floors

alt_summaries.summary: Final boss of the Trial of the Sekhemas (after all four floors) according to a guide.

name: Zerphi
summary: Vaal noble who lived to 168, a serial killer who tortured and killed thirteen noble Gemling victims over 128 years and was found rejuvenated to age twenty; his longevity prompted Atziri to order Doryani to study it.

name: Zorath, Vile Assembled
summary: Endgame pinnacle boss of the Abyss mechanic. Its arena, The Lightless Hollow, is reached directly on the Atlas; the fight begins once four Zorath's Eye fragments are placed in its head. New content in 3.29.0 per the wiki.

sources.locator: Intro: 'the endgame pinnacle boss of the Abyss mechanic'; header 'New content version=3.29.0'; Entry: 'Players must place four different Zorath's Eye fragments into Zorath's head'

name: The Abyss
summary: Cracks and pits that spawn monsters when approached; source of abyss jewels, Stygian Vises and the Abyssal Depths in PoE1 Abyss league (3.1.0); PoE2 Rise of the Abyssal (0.3.0) revives Abysses with the Well of Souls and desecration.

name: Archnemesis modifiers
summary: Itemised modifiers applied to petrified monsters to build custom rare boss fights. The wiki gives no narrative explanation.

name: Ascendancy
summary: Ascendancy classes unlock through trials. In PoE1 the Lord's Labyrinth quest leads to the Trials of Ascendancy; in PoE2 the Ascension Trials (Sekhemas, Chaos) grant ascendancy points.

sources.locator: infobox: objective 'Finish the Trials of Ascendancy to access ... Labyrinth'

alt_summaries.summary: Power granted to the exile who completes Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth trials; framed as inheriting the Labyrinth's succession test.

name: The Atlas of Worlds (concept)
summary: The endgame structure of PoE1: a web of alternate worlds ('maps') reached through the Map Device. Wiki lore says it was either found or created by the Elder as a hunting ground; after the Elder's defeat other powers (Maven, Eldritch Horrors, the Originator) contest it. PoE2 has its own, separate Atlas whose Precursor Towers are mentioned in PoE1 wiki lore.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' / 'The Elder and the Shaper'
lead: 'The Atlas of Worlds may have originally been created as a feeding ground for the Elder'

name: Atlas Passive Skill Tree
summary: The upgrade tree of the PoE1 Atlas endgame, spent with Atlas passive skill points and Atlas passive respec points. Points come from Atlas Book of Skill items and from quest rewards (for example The Elder, The Maven's Game, The Searing Exarch, The Eater of Worlds). The wiki counts 9 Atlas Books of Skill for 12 Atlas passive points in total.

sources.locator: 'List of Book of Skills' intro: 'There are 9 Atlas Book of Skills in Wraeclast, for a total of 12 Atlas passive points'; the earned points are shown by hovering over the counter 'at the bottom of the Atlas passive tree'
Walkthrough 'Use the Atlas Book of Skill' and Quest Complete log: 'gained 1 Atlas Passive Skill Point and 2 Atlas Passive Respec Points'

name: Azurite
summary: Crystal mined in Delve and spent for supplies; also the material in which Aul encased his citadel.

name: Gods as belief and Beast-energy
summary: Interpretive concept: gods in Wraeclast are sustained by worship and by proximity to the Beast's power; their abilities are 'restricted by the Beast'. Fan synthesis built from wiki statements on godhood and the Beast.

sources.locator: Lore: 'Like the other gods of Wraeclast, Kitava's abilities are restricted by the Beast'
Halani found powerless from lack of worship (see PoE1 'God' page, Maraketh gods)

name: The Beyond
summary: Plane of demons reachable via Beyond portals in Beyond league (1.2.0); Beyond demons later became a core mechanic (Beyond passives replaced Breach ones in Keepers league).

sources.locator: restrictions: Beyond passives moved to take Breach's place

name: Before Imperial Calendar (BIC)
summary: Dating convention for events preceding Imperial year 1 (e.g. Vaal fall c. 400 BIC; Vaal–Azmeri contact c. 1200 BIC).

sources.locator: The Vaal > Contacting the Azmeri; The End of Vaal Civilization (c. 400 BIC)

name: Blight (fungal growth)
summary: Fungal growths infesting Wraeclast whose mycelium spawns monster waves once a Purification Pump pierces it. Cassia first thought it a symptom of Wraeclast's death, then a parasite, and suspects a central growth that Blighted maps lead to.

name: Blightheart
summary: Hypothesised original source of the Blight. Dhunan (historical Order of the Djinn 'Blightmaster') theorised its existence; Sister Cassia independently suspects a central growth that the Blighted maps lead to. No in-game confirmation is cited.

sources.locator: member list (Dhunan) and Blight Scarabs section

name: Bloodline modifier
summary: Bloodline modifiers were shared modifiers on each pack of magic monsters in Bloodlines league; they could affect combat while the pack lived and after it died.

name: The Breach
summary: Otherworldly realm/phenomenon whose tears let Breach monsters enter Wraeclast; original Breach league (2.5.0) had breaches expanding as monsters are killed, splinters forming Breachstones for the five Breachlords' Domains. Replaced in 3.28.0 by the Keepers-of-the-Flame rework (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree). PoE2 has Unstable Breaches and the Breachlords' lore (Xesht).

sources.locator: version history 3.28.0: new Breach replaces original Breach mechanic

name: Thirteen Moons
summary: Thirteen Imperial months (Verusi, Divini, Derivi, Phreci, Caspiri, Astrali, Eterni, Atziri, Vivici, Lurici, Sagari, Vitali, Azmeri), some named for renowned figures; Wraeclast has seasons.

name: Imperial Seven-Day Week
summary: Eternal seven-day week named after components of existence: Solaro, Lunaro, Fiero, Glacio, Galvano, Kaso, Sacrato.

name: Cataclysm
summary: Lore term for the world-ending catastrophes that destroyed civilisations: the unknown cataclysm that wiped out the Precursors, the Vaal Cataclysm (also 'The Fall', c. 400 BIC), and the Eternal Empire Cataclysm (~1339 IC). The corpus uses the word for each event but does not define a single in-world category; this node groups those uses. Not the PoE2 epilogue quest 'Cataclysm's Wake', which is an Atlas tutorial quest.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era to c. 1339 IC (several events)

sources.locator: intro: 'An incredibly advanced precursor civilization existed, but was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm.'; section '====The Vaal Cataclysm====': 'The Vaal Cataclysm, also known as The Fall, was a historical event...'
section '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===': 'The Cataclysm brought an end to Voll's reign and the Eternal Empire as a whole.'
page intro: 'Cataclysm's Wake is an epilogue quest. It act as the tutorial quest for the Atlas.'

name: The Cleansing Fire
summary: Cosmic force: sentient neural network of suns and black stars seeking omniscience by disintegrating what it studies; served by the Black Star and the Searing Exarch. Its all-seeing-eye symbol resembles the descry and may be origin of Templar religion (wiki inference).

sources.locator: Lycia: 'prayed to symbol of the Cleansing Fire ... Innocence appropriated it'
Cleansing Fire section: 'omnipotent neural network of suns and black stars'; symbol 'very similar to the descry'

name: Corruption
summary: Lore force of mutation and malformation tied to the Beast and its predecessors: the Beast 'possesses corrupting powers' that mutate whatever contacts it; Kitava is called 'God of Corruption' in Karui dialogue; Precursors mastered corruption and Doryani attempts to harness the Precursor Weapon to destroy corruption. Not the Corrupted-item mechanic.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era onward (Beast, Vaal, Eternal Empire)

sources.locator: intro: 'The Beast possesses corrupting powers, devouring the souls of his prey and mutating whoever comes in contact with it.'
section '==Kitava==' > Dialogue, Haku's 'Kaom' option: 'Kitava, God of Corruption, consumed Kaom from heart to skin.'
section '===Precursor civilization===': 'After mastering corruption, they delved deeper...'; the Precursor Weapon is one 'which Doryani attempts to harness to destroy corruption'

alt_summaries.summary: The in-world corrupting power named by the Karui and Vaal (Kitava as 'God of Corruption', worship of Corruption at a Vaal temple) and carried as the Seed of Corruption (what remains of the Beast) in PoE2. The item-corruption mechanic is a separate game system.

name: Darkness (Delve)
summary: Lightless darkness in the Azurite Mine that damages unprepared delvers; requires flares; Aul and Kurgal fights include a darkness phase.

name: Day Zero rule (league narrative)
summary: Dev narrative rule: each league story begins with the exile face-down on the Twilight Strand, just exiled by Dominus, so league events cannot build on what the exile did in earlier leagues. Earlier events are attributed to other exiles or remembered as memories.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule; cites 'Integrating League Stories' and ExileCon 2019 dev talks)

name: Delirium
summary: Fog of madness released through Mirrors of Delirium that spawns and strengthens monsters and can lead to the Simulacrum. Origin is only hinted: Kalandra links it to 'the Trickster' and PoE2 ties Tangmazu to a tutorial Delirium encounter.

name: Delirium: The Hare and the Raven
summary: 0.5 Delirium storyline ('The Hare and the Raven' in the press release): Elder Madox is freed from a Delirium mirror (Strange Reflection), leads the Exile to the Withered Willow, and the Raven Trickster Tangmazu must be stopped. Official notes: 'An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed, spreading madness across Wraeclast.'

sources.locator: Delirium (The Hare and the Raven): confrontation with Tangmazu
An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed

name: Essence
summary: Imprisoned essences freed in Essence league (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds); modify items with guaranteed affixes; can be corrupted (Hysteria, Delirium, Horror, Insanity).

name: Exile (exile system)
summary: The exile system: criminals of Oriath are sentenced by the Templar government and shipped to Wraeclast. The sentence text reads 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. The player's character is one of these exiles. Precedent exists: under Tyndarus Phrecius, people were exiled to the land later called Trarthus. The wiki gives no single in-world reason for choosing Wraeclast.

sources.locator: section 'The Present'; section 'Reign of Tyndarus Phrecius' (Trarthus exile)

name: Exile's Journey (Day Zero rule)
summary: The wiki's 'Day Zero' rule: each league's narrative starts with the Exile face-down in the sand of the Twilight Strand, having just been exiled by Dominus, so league stories cannot build on earlier leagues' events.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule)

name: Forsaken Masters
summary: Seven NPC masters introduced in Forsaken Masters (1.2.0): Elreon, Haku, Vorici, Vagan, Tora, Leo and Catarina (plus Zana); they vanished at Betrayal, taken by the Syndicate (all but Zana).

name: Fragmented Memory
summary: Decaying memory sub-zones found throughout Wraeclast in Synthesis; some are memories of real events (e.g. Malachai's slave mines, gemling experiments, the Templar Laboratory) and are used by the wiki as lore sources.

sources.locator: citations of 'Abandoned Shaft Memory' and 'Eternal Residence Memory'

name: Nature of godhood (ascension)
summary: In PoE lore a mortal of rare quality could ascend to godhood on the adoration of their people, shedding mortality; this became impossible once Sin created the Beast. Becoming a god often costs one's humanity. Gods can also be 'made' by belief of followers (Innocence's ascension was fuelled by hatred of Sin).

chronology.relative: before the creation of the Beast

sources.locator: Sin, 'The Origins of the Gods': "There was a time before the Beast ... men and women like you could ascend. Through rareness of quality and the adoration of their people..."

name: Harbinger
summary: Otherworldly enemies of Harbinger league (3.0.0) beaten by killing their minions; drop currency shards.

name: Heart of the Grove
summary: Plant that grows from a harvested Tier 4 Sacred Grove seed (about 100 growth cycles). Harvesting it is the challenge that leads to the Avatar of the Grove; Oshabi herself turns into it after the tutorial quest.

sources.locator: League mechanic: Heart of the Grove
Lead: Oshabi turns into the Heart of the Grove

name: Eternal calendar
summary: Calendar of 1 IC (Imperialis Conceptus), seven days and thirteen moons (Verusi, Divini, Derivi ... Azmeri).

name: Eternal slave trade
summary: Under Chitus the Empire enslaved Karui, Ezomytes and Maraketh, sending them to mines and cities.

name: Intrinsic darkness
summary: Tane's term for the cruelty/ill-will in living beings that Metamorphs distil from monster organs; he now thinks it older and more universal than Corruption and hopes to destroy it while leaving the flesh unharmed.

name: Kalguuran runesmithing
summary: Kalguuran art of engraving starlight runes (Verisium from meteorites) into weapons and armour; Ezomytes learned it from the first expedition; revived as Runesmithing in Settlers and Runeforging in PoE2 Act 4.

name: Karui Gods
summary: The gods honoured within the Karui Way: Arohongui, Hinekora, Kitava, Ngamahu, Ramako, Tasalio, Tawhoa, Tukohama and Valako, as named on the Karui Gods page.

sources.locator: intro: 'In the game's lore, The Karui Way has several gods that are representative of or rule over various aspects of the world.'

name: Karui Way (Makanui)
summary: Karui code of honour and traditions (Way of the Warrior); some who follow it forbid virtue gems for causing blood fever.

name: The Kingsmarch Charter
summary: Royal charter under which Kingsmarch operates; Johan enforces it to the letter, including punishments such as the Royal Order of Criminal Hanging subject to a statute of limitations.

name: Kingsmarch shipping and trade routes
summary: Trade shipping from Kingsmarch to Kalguuran ports (Riben Fell, Pondium, Kalguur) and Karui ports (Ngakanu, Te Onui, Moti Aro); risks include pirates, corrupt officials, a royal tax and 'mysterious green light' losses. Pirate Admiral Valerius can commandeer ships.

name: Kingsmarch workers and town management
summary: Recruited workers (miners, smelters, farmers, disenchanters, shippers, Atlas runners) are hired through Raulf for Gold; the town runs on real-time resources: ores, bars, crops and thaumaturgic dust.

name: Lifeforce
summary: Oshabi's name for the invisible force that revives the dead and shapes beasts and plants, released by Grove seeds in Wild, Vivid and Primal forms; she notes its similarity to Corruption and calls them perhaps 'two sides of the same leaf'.

sources.locator: Dialogue: Lifeforce, The Slaying of Malachai, Monsters

name: Lord's Trial
summary: Azmerian maze-festival to choose chieftains; raised Veruso to power and inspired Izaro's Labyrinth.

name: Memory Tears and Threads
summary: Tears in Atlas reality where Zana's manifested memories leak; Eagon traces threads to Moments of Loneliness, Trauma, Reverence.

name: Nemesis modifier
summary: Nemesis modifiers were powerful extra modifiers on every rare monster in Nemesis league (hardcore); the league modifier was "Rare Monsters each have a Nemesis Mod".

name: The Pantheon
summary: Pantheon power system introduced by Sin after Tukohama's death: Sin captures the souls of the risen gods the exile kills in Part Two and lends the exile a small portion of their power. The Brine King, Arakaali, Solaris and Lunaris grant major god powers; Tukohama, Abberath, Ryslatha, Ralakesh, Gruthkul, Yugul, Garukhan and Shakari are minor gods.

sources.locator: After Tukohama: Sin introduces the Pantheon
'Sin is able to capture the souls of the Pantheon of gods'
Garukhan is a minor pantheon goddess

name: Prophecy
summary: Prophecy system of Prophecy league (2.3.0); removed in 3.17.0; Pale Council bosses.

name: The Red Pyre
summary: Entity/title in Ailith's Word of the Dreamer ('The Red Pyre burns hot... The Dreamer once knew him, before his addiction'). The fire imagery and the book's subject (the four Breachlords that became Xesht) point to Xoph, Dark Embers; the identification is inferred, not stated.

name: Ritual (altar mechanic)
summary: Ritual Altars spawn wave encounters inside a ritual circle; defeating monsters earns Favour/Tribute to buy items. PoE1 Ritual league gives no narrative; Vaal Ritual Altars may summon Atziri's Apparition; later Wildwood lore ties 'ritual altars' to the King in the Mists; PoE2 adopts it in Forbidden Rites.

name: Rogue exiles
summary: Exiled criminals who roam Wraeclast as hostile NPCs; originated in Anarchy league (0.11.0), later reused in PoE2 (Lichborn exiles in Rise of the Abyssal).

sources.locator: raising a rogue exile as Lichborn

name: Royal Order of Criminal Hanging
summary: A royal order to hang named criminals that was damaged by seawater on the voyage to Kingsmarch; Johan declined to enforce it because the reply would exceed the Charter's statute of limitations and he would not hang the wrong man.

sources.locator: ==Legal Response (Johan)==: "the recent Royal Order of Criminal Hanging was damaged by seawater"; "the punishment in question will exceed the Charter statute of limitations"

name: Sekhema
summary: Maraketh leader title; always a woman chosen by merit and anointed with the feather of the Great Roc; tale-women keep the people's history.

name: Shrine (Domination)
summary: Shrines are a mechanic introduced by Domination league (1.0.0); Domination's area modifier allowed shrines to spawn.

sources.locator: lead: 'This league introduced shrines'; Modifier section

name: Strongbox
summary: Strongboxes are a mechanic introduced by Ambush league (1.1.0, March 2014); every area in Ambush carried the Ambush chests modifier.

name: Tempest
summary: Tempests are effects introduced by Tempest league that can change monster and player size, cause damage, alter drop rates, or animate weapons that drop; affected areas are shown on the World Screen.

name: Thaumaturgy
summary: Gem-based magic whose source is the Beast. Outlawed by Veruso, embraced by Chitus under Malachai's 'Thaumatocracy', and banned again by Voll.

name: The Decay
summary: Ancient cosmic mould-like entity ('the Oblivion') from outside time and space that turns all it touches to void; the Elder is its servant. Dormant after the Elder's defeat.

name: The Pantheon (soul-capture mechanic)
summary: Game mechanic and lore device by which Sin captures the essences of slain gods and grants the Exile a fraction of their powers. Major gods: Brine King, Arakaali, Solaris, Lunaris. Minor gods: Tukohama, Abberath, Ryslatha (Act 6), Gruthkul, Ralakesh (Act 7), Yugul (Act 8), Garukhan, Shakari (Act 9).

sources.locator: section 'The Pantheon'; Sin dialogue 'The Father of War': "While a god may fall, their essence lingers... That essence can be yours"

name: The Struggle
summary: Ancient conflict among cosmic forces (the Decay, the Tangle, the Cleansing Fire) introduced by the Envoy. The forces cannot clash directly without rending reality, so disputes are settled by duels between mortal champions. The Elder's defeat left a vacancy over the Atlas that drew the others in; the Maven, with the Exile as her champion and Kirac's Vanguard, stands against the Eldritch champions. A progenitor/Lightkeeper is cited as the order the forces are blind to.

sources.locator: lead: 'defeat of the Elder ... created a temporary vacancy'

name: The Tangle
summary: Cosmic force served by the Infinite Hunger and the Eater of Worlds (flavour: sea of limbs, to eat, to feast).

name: Timeless Conflict
summary: Legions of different factions (Karui, Maraketh, Templar, Eternal Empire, Vaal) frozen in stasis by a timeless monolith, locked in an endless battle; broken out of stasis by damaging them. Why they are frozen is not explained in the wiki.

name: Tormented spirits
summary: Spirits of tormented criminals in Torment league (1.3.0) that flee, empower nearby monsters and drop loot; unrelated to Kitava's Torments in Act 5.

name: Trial of Chaos
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 3 at the Temple of Chaos via an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the quest item Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian). Based on the PoE1 Ultimatum league and overseen by the Trialmaster.

sources.locator: intro: 'The Trialmaster ... oversee the Trials of Chaos'

alt_summaries.summary: Ascension trial in the Temple of Chaos (first in Act 3), a gauntlet run with an Inscribed Ultimatum; the Trialmaster offers modifiers and rewards. Mechanically based on PoE1's Ultimatum.

name: Trial of the Sekhemas
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 2 via the Djinn Barya key (or the quest item Balbala's Barya), a gauntlet of up to 4 floors with bosses including Rattlecage, Hadi and Rafiq, Ashar and Zarokh.

alt_summaries.summary: Ascension trial first accessible in Act 2 via a Djinn Barya on the Relic Altar; a gauntlet governed by Honour, Boons and Afflictions; based on PoE1's Forbidden Sanctum.

name: Uber pinnacle bosses
summary: Harder repeatable versions: Uber Elder, Uber Sirus, Uber Maven, Uber Exarch/Eater after 24 influenced T14+ maps. Memory-version retellings per Day Zero.

name: Vaal corruption and thaumaturgical technology
summary: Vaal science combined gem-craft, constructs, mechanical technology and corruption drawn from the Beast; much of it was developed by Doryani and housed at Atzoatl and Utzaal. Its influence resurfaces as Vaal side areas, Vaal skill gems and Vaal Orbs in PoE1.

name: Vaal sacrifice and Vaal souls
summary: Vaal bloodpriests discovered that the souls of the recently killed briefly seek another source of life and can be captured in a vaal skill gem to empower it; human and blood sacrifice powered Vaal constructs and society, and slavery supplied victims.

name: Verisium
summary: Metal ore found only in fallen meteorites and not native to Wraeclast; Kalguuran runes were typically crafted from it, and in PoE2 Act 4 Dannig forges Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots.

sources.locator: ===Runes===: "Runes were typically crafted using Verisium, a type of metal ore found only from fallen meteorites, and not native to Wraeclast."
Bring the Verisium to Dannig / Take the Verisium Spikes from Dannig: Dannig crafts Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots
Remnants can contain Verisium used in Runeforging
Seek out the crater of a fallen star, a meteor of pure Verisium

alt_summaries.summary: Ore from remnants and a meteor; enables Runeforging and Runic Ward.

name: Virtue Gems
summary: Gems from the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy, buried by Veruso and mined by slaves under Chitus; infused into gemlings. Ubiquitous in Vaal society.

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri term for virtue gems, which they are forbidden to touch; contact causes a horrific reaction.
Gems discovered under Mount Veruso that the Vaal used to gain great power; Vaal bodies were adorned and later socketed with gems, and the Vaal never shared the secret with the Azmeri.

name: Wildwood ascendancy classes
summary: Affliction's temporary ascendancies (Wildwood Primalist with charms, Warden of the Maji with tinctures, Warlock of the Mists with corpse items) earned through the Azmeri questlines; removed at league end.

name: Humours / Wisps (Wildwood)
summary: In the Viridian Wildwood the four humours (Primal, Vivid, Wild, Sacred) materialise as wisps. The first three share names with Harvest's Primal, Vivid and Wild Lifeforce colours. Sacred humours are harvested by the ritual altars of the King in the Mists.

name: Hiveborn
summary: Breach-spawn into which the Breachlords were evolving; the Keepers of the Flame, founded through Chayula's dreams, exist to destroy them. The Dreamer is revealed to be of the same kind as the Hiveborn.

sources.locator: Lore: the Breachlords began their evolution into the Hiveborn; the Dreamer is the same creature as the Hiveborn

alt_summaries.summary: Mutated Breach monsters spilling into Wraeclast through a stabilised interdimensional link.
Breach monsters invading Wraeclast in the reworked Breach; fought by the Exile and Ailith, source of Graftblood and Hiveblood.

name: Kitava's Heart
summary: A part of Kitava that spawns during its battle in Act 5 (Cathedral Rooftop, The Feeding Trough) and Act 10. Introduced as a boss monster in 3.0.0; since 3.2.0 it cannot be slowed below its base speed.

sources.locator: lead: 'Kitava's Heart is a part of Kitava that spawns during the battle with Kitava, the Insatiable, which occurs in Act 5 and Act 10'; Version history 3.0.0 'Introduced to the game as boss monster'; 3.2.0 speed note

name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
summary: Ancient subterranean race created, not born, via necromancy, afraid of light; invaded during the Winter of the World and were driven back underground by the returning sun. Antagonists of Abyss and PoE2 Rise of the Abyssals.

sources.locator: The Winter of the World > The Lightless

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient necromantic race, the Abyssals ('the spawn of the Well of Souls' per the Hooded One), serving Kulemak through Lich Lords; they emerge through Abyss fissures. Ancient alliances fought them for centuries in the Winter of the World.

name: Metamorph
summary: Shape-shifting enemies assembled from organs of other monsters and bosses; they use the moves of whatever parts they carry.

name: Scourge monsters
summary: Blood-crazed demonic monsters of the Scourge Nightmare realm. After the league they became the core game's Beyond monsters, and currencies such as Tainted Blessing came from them.

name: Synthetes
summary: Synthesis league bosses (Altered, Augmented, Rewritten and Twisted Synthete) guarding fractured uniques; later unique-map bosses.

sources.locator: unique items paragraph listing Altered/Augmented/Rewritten/Twisted Synthete

name: The Titans
summary: Primordial race that walked molten Wraeclast and inhabited its volcanoes; mostly indifferent to humans; nearly wiped out in the 'rising darkness', with the Molten One the sole survivor.

name: Trarthan mercenaries
summary: Lawless Trarthan veterans met in Mercenaries league; hirable allies with unique gear and skills; noble ones come from the four Great Houses.

name: The Undying
summary: Gemlings and citizens of Sarn transformed by the Cataclysm into mindless monsters that can live for centuries; some gemling legionnaires later regain sentience (Act 8 Grain Gate).

name: Vorniculia / horrors
summary: Horror species that attacked Kalguuran outposts; Olroth's Knights culled the Vorniculia.

name: Wisps (humours)
summary: Wildwood humours materialised as Primal, Vivid, Wild and Sacred wisps; freed wisps escape into the overworld empowering monsters; Sacred humours are harvested by the King in the Mists' ritual altars.

name: Abberath, the Cloven One
summary: Goatman god (the Cloven One, Quaffer of Souls) killed in the Valley of the Fire Drinker. Per Bestel, goatmen offer him humans and he eats them 'meat, soul and all'; per Sin he was once Abberath the Scholar King, an alchemist who burned flesh away to drink the life force within, starting with goats. Minor Pantheon god.

sources.locator: Bestel: 'when the goatmen find him a ... human... he eats them'
Act 6 dialogue "Abberath": the Scholar King, Quaffer of Souls

alt_summaries.summary: Former scholar who consumed souls of goats and became the goat-like Cloven One; father of the Faun; Act 6 Pantheon boss.

name: Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows
summary: Vaal spider-goddess of love and death, worshipped by Azmeri artists; consorts with Silk in the Temple of Decay and is killed as Act 7's boss. A relationship with Sin is hinted.

sources.locator: 'lesser relationships with ... Arakaali' (cites PoE2 Arakaali's Lust)

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal harlot turned fertility goddess and queen, the Spinner of Shadows; held Sin captive; sealed in the Temple of Decay and slain by the Exile in Act 7.
Spinner of Shadows: mortal temptress turned arachnid, Vaal goddess of fertility, first worshipped by the Azmeri; her temple is the Temple of Decay (Act 7).

name: Arohongui, Daughter of the Moon
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. Daughter of Ramako's alleged impersonator and Sione; lacks the warmth and light of the Sun

alt_summaries.summary: Karui moon goddess, Daughter of the Moon; daughter of Ramako and Lani Lua in myth (possibly Tangmazu's child).

name: The Beast
summary: Divine creature, source of thaumaturgy and corruption, grown by Sin from the Dark Ember beneath Highgate to keep the gods asleep. Has no will of its own; exploited by Doryani, Atziri, Chitus, Malachai. The Exile kills it in Act 4; PoE2 follows a new Beast grown from the stolen Seed of Corruption.

alt_summaries.summary: Gigantic Dark Ember creature sealed under Highgate, killed by the Exile in Act 4; its death weakens the gods' restraint.
Gods-lulling Dark Ember creature killed in Act 4.

Creature grown by Sin from the Dark Ember to lull the gods into sleep and prevent mortal ascension to godhood; killed by the exile in Act 4, which freed the gods and the souls of Malachai's lieutenants.
Ancient divine creature grown from the Seed of Corruption by Sin; in PoE2 a Beast carried across the Vastiri on the Faridun Dreadnought and fed corpses by the Countess's plan.
Ancient divine creature of thaumaturgy, created by Sin from the Seed of Corruption; Atziri and Doryani manipulated it.

name: The Brine King
summary: Azmeri king Tsoagoth turned god of storms and sea, worshipped by the Brinerot pirates with sacrifices; Act 6 Pantheon boss.

sources.locator: Nessa: 'his majesty could never be satiated on his wedding day by one bride alone'

alt_summaries.summary: Sea god who turns Nessa into a mermaid to wed her; Act 6 final boss in his reef, whose domain was the city of Tsoatha.

name: Chaos
summary: Impulse able to see across timelines, once worshipped by Vaal priests; master of the Trialmaster and enemy-of-sorts to Hinekora's fixed prophecies.

sources.locator: intro and section 'Interactions with other characters'
Community Team post: 'Chaos does not know what you truly are...'

alt_summaries.summary: An Impulse, a beyond-godlike being and the flip of the coin, who can see multiple timelines and is the master of the Trialmaster. Worshipped by the Vaal. The Blood Crucible was a pact between Chaos and the Vaal High Priests.

Impulse, a godlike entity that sees all possibilities across timelines and delights in mortals bending chance; once worshipped by the Vaal; master of the Trialmaster; opposed to Order. Aware that the exiles exist in parallel timelines (dev statement).

Impulse of Chaos, not a Vaal god, but a sect of Vaal priests worshipped him; his Temple of Chaos stood on the outskirts of Utzaal. The Trialmaster says Atziri's realm lies beyond his reach and the Vaal fall occurred in every timeline.

name: Chayula, the Dreamer
summary: Breachlord known as the Dreamer or Benevolent Dreamer; PoE2 lore shows he aided the Third Pact alliance, was severed from the failed Breachlord merge, and formed the Keepers of the Flame through dreams. After Xesht falls Ailith reveals his ultimate aim is to subjugate all life as obedient thralls.

sources.locator: Lore: the Dreamer is Chayula, a Breachlord
Lore: after Xesht is defeated Ailith tells the player the Dreamer's true intent

alt_summaries.summary: One of five Breachlords (chaos). Boss of Chayula's Domain (male per wiki). As the Dreamer (Keepers league) he opposes the Xesht fusion. Original Breach bosses introduced in 2.5.0 (Chayula to the core game 2.6.0 per wiki version history), removed 3.28.0.
Breachlord worshipped at Atzoatl by the Cult of Purple Flame.

name: Craiceann, First of the Deep
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Deep ('First of All'), ancestor of crabs, squid and sea creatures; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the deep.

name: The Eater of Worlds
summary: Eldritch Horror serving the Tangle, fought in Absence of Symmetry and Harmony.

name: Esh, Forked Thought
summary: One of five Breachlords. Lightning damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Esh's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

sources.locator: boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other

alt_summaries.summary: Breachlord (Esh) fought as a paired boss with its counterpart in the Hive Colony (PoE2 0.5); they share a health bar in the final phase and drop the Breachlord Sac.

name: Farrul, First of the Plains
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Plains ('First of the Hunt'), ancestor of hounds, cats and other mammals; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the plains.

name: Fenumus, First of the Night
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Night ('First Explorer'), ancestor of bugs and insectoids; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the night; wove a net during the Great Fire.

name: Garukhan
summary: Goddess of wind and sky, formerly the Maraketh Sekhema Orbala ('Sekhema of Sekhemas'); freed Sin from the cliff where Innocence's followers had chained him, became his lover and wife and bore Shakari; Sin planted the Dark Ember 'for Garukhan'.

sources.locator: 'Garukhan, Queen of the Wind' (Orbala; Chains of Castigation, Blood of Innocence, Sin 'Garukhan' dialogue)
Relationships: Sin was wed to Garukhan

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh storm goddess, Queen of the Winds; wife of Sin, mother of Shakari; formerly the hero Orbala, Sekhema of Sekhemas (PoE2). Slain by the Exile in Act 9 at Sin's request.

Maraketh goddess ('Vulture of the Wastes', Queen of the Winds), wife of Sin and mother of Shakari; in PoE2 she is revealed to have been the mortal Sekhema Orbala. Killed in the Quarry in Act 9 after Kira's attempted sacrifice of Oyun. Minor Pantheon god.

The PoE1 wiki's Orbala page says PoE2 identifies Garukhan as the ascended Orbala (mortal Maraketh warrior); the PoE1 wiki and PoE2 quests do not fully confirm this, so it stays inferred. The Horn of the Vastiri quest retraces Orbala's footsteps.

name: The God of Domination
summary: Mysterious, possibly otherworldly god tied to the Harbingers; Harbinger uniques foretell its gaze falling over Wraeclast.

name: The Goddess of Justice
summary: Deity worshipped by Izaro Phrecius; known only by this title.

name: The Greatwolf
summary: First Ones-type god of the hunt and ancestor of wolves and werewolves; possessed Rigwald, the Wolven King, during the Purity Rebellion.

alt_summaries.summary: Ezomyte First One that possessed Thane Rigwald after he sought its power in the Purity Rebellion.

name: Gruthkul
summary: Bestial minor god, Mother of Despair / Porcelain Queen, a mother whose children were slaughtered by Arakaali and whose grief made her a horned beast; Act 7 Pantheon boss. Sources disagree on the culprit: the God page says Arakaali slaughtered her children; Sin's dialogue says the Vaal laid waste to her kingdom; Sin's 'Mother of Despair' dialogue says her daughters plotted against Arakaali.

sources.locator: Sin: 'The Vaal laid waste to her kingdom and placed her slaughtered children at her feet.'
Act 7 dialogue "The Mother of Despair": the daughters plotted against Arakaali

alt_summaries.summary: Grieving mother-goddess whose kingdom the Vaal laid waste and whose children were slaughtered; mad with the wish to share her grief, she is killed in the Den of Despair (Dread Thicket). Sin hints that her daughters had plotted against Arakaali, who left her web only when forced to. Minor Pantheon god.

name: Hinekora
summary: Karui goddess, the Mother of Death, ruler of the Halls of the Dead, seer of prophecy; speaks through the Well of Passing and rewards the worthy with the Tattoo of Hinekora.

sources.locator: Peer into the Well of Passing

alt_summaries.summary: Karui Mother of Death; collects souls in the Halls of the Dead, foresees events across timelines, whipped Kitava into the underworld with her hair, and slept after foreseeing the Slumbering of the Gods. Oversees the Trial of the Ancestors.
Karui goddess of death; could not see Doryani in the past.

name: Innocence
summary: Templar god of light and purity, twin of Sin; per Lycia's relics his ascension was fuelled by turning followers against Sin. In Act 5 High Templar Avarius is his vessel; after Sin's 'more sensible host' (Bannon) sacrifices himself with the Staff of Purity in Act 10, he is reborn, helps defeat Kitava and then goes into self-exile in the far south.

sources.locator: section 'Lore' (Innocence defeated in Act 5; re-awakened by Bannon for Act 10)
Avarius as vessel of Innocence (see Kitava page: Triumph of Innocence)
quest An End to Hunger/Death and Rebirth: Bannon resurrects Innocence
Lore: stained glass windows, Original Sin
Bannon: 'it has the ability to revitalize Innocence into waking fully'
Innocence: "Bone and corruption shall not impede the path of purity!"

alt_summaries.summary: The god the Templars worship as saviour. Sin captures Innocence's soul; Avarius becomes its vessel and Innocence is defeated in Act 5. Re-awakened by Bannon's sacrifice, it helps defeat Kitava in Act 10.
Templar god, twin of Sin; ascended using hatred of Sin; Oriath's founding deity; also Maxarius.
Templar god of purity, twin brother of Sin; his vessel Avarius is killed by the Exile; his fall allows Kitava's summoning.
Sin's twin brother and a Templar god; hosted by High Templar Avarius, destroyed in Act 5 and in Act 10 resurrected when Bannon sacrifices himself, then destroys Kitava's Horns to help the exile.

name: Kamasa
summary: Vaal god of Wealth, represented by a monkey; in PoE2 Act 3 monkey-statue temples in Utzaal hold Kamasa treasure.

sources.locator: Orb of Sacrifice named for Kamasa

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal Monkey God of wealth and greed; mentioned in PoE2 Act 2/3 and in PoE1 items.

name: Kitava
summary: Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption (Father of Corruption, the Cannibal King, Black Spirit); invited into Wraeclast by the Eternals per Karui lore, devours Oriath and is slain by the Exile with Sin and Innocence in Act 10.

sources.locator: Lore: 'Karui god of chaos, hunger, and corruption'; final boss of Act 5 and Act 10

alt_summaries.summary: The Karui god of destruction, who awakens after Innocence is defeated. Killed in Act 10 with Sin and a re-awakened Innocence, after Bannon's sacrifice.
Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption; summoned by Utula at the end of Act 5; the Exile cannot defeat him until Act 10.
Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption, a cannibal deity who feeds on Oriath; reawakens at the end of Act 5, is the final boss of Acts 5 and 10 and is killed in the Feeding Trough.

name: Kopec
summary: Vaal sun god; the Temple of Kopec in Utzaal sealed the time gateway.

sources.locator: Alva: 'Temple of the Sun God, Kopec'

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal god, presumably of sun or fire; PoE2 has the Temple of Kopec.

name: Kulemak
summary: Master of the Lightless and creator of the Lich Lords; exalted within the Well of Souls (which arose after The Master Below All 'raged'), he waged the Winter of the World against the surface until the Three Sisters destroyed his mortal form; his soul returned to the Well. Namesake of the Horns of Kulemak (Immortal Syndicate). PoE2 pinnacle of the Well of Souls content.

sources.locator: Hooded One: 'Kulemak, the Lich Lord, master of Undeath'

alt_summaries.summary: Creator and master of the Lightless and Lich Lords; exalted within the Well of Souls (power of necromancy); waged war on the surface, deceived Aul with a bargain for a stone golem, ending the primeval civilisation. Destroyed in mortal form by the Three Sisters; his soul returned to the Well. Appears in PoE2 (Rise of the Abyssal / Abyss).
Abyssal god of undeath whose Well of Souls is in Act 2; lieutenants Amanamu, Ulaman and Kurgal; the Lurking Creature calls Sin 'Stealer of Kulemak's spark'. Relevant to endgame via Tecrod.

Lich Lord, creator and master of the Lightless, exalted in the Well of Souls; the Hooded One calls him 'a dark god... Kulemak, the Lich Lord, master of Undeath' whose body the alliance destroyed countless times though the Well stayed out of reach. Fought as the Vessel of Kulemak via Kulemak's Invitation in the Black Cathedral.

name: Lani Lua
summary: Karui Mother of the Moon (the Karui sister name for the lunar goddess), involved in the myth of Ramako and Arohongui. Note: The Three Sisters page lists Lani Lua as sun and Sione as moon, contradicting the God page (Lani Lua moon, Sione sun); the wiki is inconsistent.

sources.locator: Karui: Lani Lua (sun), Sione (moon) - wiki lists them in this order; conflicts with Karui Gods page

name: The Lightkeeper (the Progenitor)
summary: Progenitor figure named by the Envoy: the Cleansing Fire is blind to 'the path set before it by the lightkeeper'; Struggle page says he tests the limits of limitless power and directs the weavers of destiny. Nature and relation to the Maven unresolved.

name: Lunaris
summary: Eternal/Azmeri moon goddess, sister of Solaris; her rivalry was engineered by Tangmazu. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)

alt_summaries.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.
Azmerian god of the Moon, sister of Solaris and Viridi, worshipped by the Eternal Empire; fought alongside Solaris at the Harbour Bridge in Act 8 after the Moon Orb is taken from Dusk.

name: The Master Below All
