summary: Warlords of Trarthus were executed after Phrecian legions occupied it; four first-generation Trarthans led a war; Karui blockades and Ezomyte sabotage doomed reinforcements; Tyndarus capitulated after two years.

name: Trarthan War of Independence
summary: 870-872 IC rebellion against Tyndarus.

name: Trial of the Ancestors
summary: Tournament in the Halls of the Dead where the Exile's team of Karui warriors fights teams led by the ten Karui chieftains, destroying totems; winning a full tournament earns rewards from Hinekora (omens, Hinekora's Lock, unique items).

sources.locator: 'rules over the Halls of the Dead and oversees the Trial of the Ancestors'

name: Trials of Chaos
summary: Escalating wave trials in which a Trialmaster-set modifier is added each round; the player banks or risks rewards. PoE1 Ultimatum league (3.14), core in 3.23; PoE2 Ascension Trial of Chaos (Act 3 Temple of Chaos, up to 10 trials).

name: Destruction of the Triskelion Flame
summary: In defeating Olroth the exile cannot save the Flame, which was keeping him alive; Dannig asks the exile to keep this from the settlers.

name: Loss of the Triskelion Flame
summary: The starlight barrier vanished as Vorana tried to adjust it; the Flame's altar was empty and all harbour ships but one had been burned. Vorana branded Uhtred a traitor, and Olroth's glass case was found empty. Uhtred had fled to an ancient shrine.

name: Turning the Tide
summary: Endgame Curse of the Allflame quest required to unlock Velka, the Tide Witch: Vesper imbues the Exile with the Allflame to pass Velka's barrier, then the Exile defeats Velka and retrieves her Allflame.

sources.locator: Quest infobox: start 'Explore a Kishara's Rest chart', objective 'Defeat Velka and retrieve her Allflame', act 'Epilogue'; Walkthrough: 'Allow me to imbue you with the power of the Allflame'

name: Vaal first contact with the Azmeri
summary: Around 1160 BC (Trinian, writing c. 1333 IC, says about 2,500 years earlier) the Vaal first contacted the primitive Azmeri tribes of the Azmerian ranges, introducing agriculture and literacy and helping create the first Azmerian written language, while never divulging the secret of virtue gems.

chronology.relative: c. 1160 BC (~2,500 years before Chitus, per Trinian)

sources.locator: section 'Contacting the Azmeri'; Trinian, The Ancients Book 4

name: Vaal Cataclysm
summary: Event c. 400 BIC that ended the Vaal Empire: Doryani's project to grant immortality (manipulating the Beast, corruption, gems, sacrifice and 'communion') went wrong; only 3,126 Vaal survived and took refuge with the Azmeri. PoE2 shows the Red Communion and Atziri being swallowed by the Beast.

sources.locator: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' (paragraph on Path of Exile 2: Fate of the Vaal)
Abilities: 'cutscene... swallowed by the Beast and starting the Cataclysm'

alt_summaries.summary: Doryani's attempt at immortality under Queen Atziri destroys the Vaal Empire. Only 3,126 Vaal survive, and they are absorbed into the Azmeri. In PoE2's Fate of the Vaal league the Exile travels back in time, with Doryani's help, to the moment before the Cataclysm.

name: Survivors among the Azmeri
summary: The 3,126 surviving Vaal found refuge among the Azmeri, could not explain what happened, had no gems and assimilated until none remained; they panicked at an image of a gem shown by the Kalguur.

name: Vastiri Becomes a Desert
summary: Over thousands of years the plains' rivers dried and forests became sand, naturally or via Maraketh/Halani-linked causes; the Maraketh became semi-nomadic.

name: Ban on collecting virtue gems in Kalguur
summary: After the Azmeri reacted fearfully to virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third officially banned their collection; the gems never returned to Kalguur (Kalguur page, Thaumaturgy section).

chronology.relative: during the reign of Cadigan III (ancient Kalguur)

sources.locator: ===Thaumaturgy===: "after witnessing the Azmeris' fearful reaction towards virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third had officially banned their collection"

name: Voll crowned Emperor
summary: Voll of Thebrus crowned Emperor in Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC (Eternal Empire page: a week after Cadiro's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci; Purity Chronicles Book 1 says the 2nd Sacrato of Phreci).

name: Voll's pact with Deshret
summary: Voll promises Sekhema Deshret the return of the Vastiri Plains for Maraketh support; she demands Titucius' skin for a saddle.

name: Voll's pact with Kaom
summary: Voll and Victario visit Kaom in Ngamakanui; Voll promises Karui sovereignty over Wraeclast's south shore and freedom for slaves in exchange for attacking Lioneye's Watch.

name: Winter of the World
aliases: Winter of the World (Great Fire / Great Wasting)
summary: Ancient war in which Kulemak and the Lightless blanketed the Vastiri Plains and the surface, ended when the Three Sisters (Solerai/Lundara etc.) destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun.

sources.locator: paragraph 1: 'Winter of the World ... lasted for centuries'
Great Fire: 'revealed that the Great Fire was indeed the same event as the Winter of the World'

alt_summaries.summary: Volcanic eruptions fill the sky with ash. The Lightless attack destroys the primeval civilization, fells the Titans and devastates the Maraketh and Azmeri. The Order of the Djinn later defeats the Lightless.
Initial Abyssal (Lightless) invasion of the surface, ended by the Three Sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun. Minimal node; fuller entry owned by another domain.
Ancient cataclysm of ash, fire and Lightless invasion; PoE2 confirmed the Ezomyte Great Fire is the same event. PoE1 wiki says it was likely caused by the Fourth Edict.

name: Zana the Originator Fractures the Atlas
summary: After the Incarnation of Dread, Zana tells Eagon she must destroy the Atlas, 'I am the catalyst', fracturing it into four quadrants and burning its pages; 3.28.0 rendering visible as the destroyed Atlas.

sources.locator: Witness Zana and Eagon; Rewards 3.28 image

name: Doryani's investigation of Zerphi
summary: Atziri ordered Doryani to research Zerphi's rejuvenation 'within the realms of possibility... without fear of question or consequence'; Vaal aged 16-26 were sent to him and none survived, the experiments failing.

name: The Afarud
summary: Rogue Faridun sect that torments djinn; led by figures such as Ridan, Afarud Commander.

alt_summaries.summary: Outcasts of the Faridun who use forbidden rites and seek destruction of Maraketh and Faridun alike, led by Saresh.

name: Azmeri
summary: Ancient tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who worship Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi and others. Eighty thousand of them under Tarcus Veruso descended into the former Vaal lands and founded the Eternal Empire in 1 IC; the Azmeri of the Forest Encampment and the Wildwood descend from those who stayed behind.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the oldest peoples of Wraeclast from the Azmerian Ranges; first lettered by the Vaal, worshipped Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi; their migrants founded the Eternal Empire (only pre-1 IC history counts as 'Azmerian'); Maji remnants in the Wildwood.
Wildwood people.
Tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who took in the Vaal survivors.

name: Bandit Lords
summary: Three rival exile bandit leaders extorting the Forest Encampment.

name: Black Scythe
summary: Kalguuran mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana, responsible for the expedition's defence and offence. Their artifacts are the currency of the Expedition NPC Tujen.

alt_summaries.summary: Mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana.

name: Black Scythes
summary: Kalguuran mercenaries led by Vorana, fighting horrors from walls with crossbows.

name: Brinerot
summary: Pirate/whaler warband of the sea whose corsairs ambush chart-seekers; their Shamanessa Velka traffics with the dead.

alt_summaries.summary: Pirates who worship the Brine King and drown mutineers or slaves.

name: Brotherhood of Silence
summary: Assassins-for-hire based primarily in Sarn, also called the Silent Brotherhood. The wiki says it acted as a hit squad for many of the Eternal Empire's elite (business with Cadiro and the Perandus family), framed Jorgin for his brother's death so he was exiled from Ogham, and surrounded Drusus in the Bath House until he drowned himself. Listed members: Shadow (former), Coralito and Vorici.

sources.locator: lead paragraph: 'faction of assassins-for-hire based primarily in Sarn'; section 'Lore': 'acted as a hit squad for many of the elite of the Eternal Empire' and the Jorgin and Drusus incidents. Era is not dated on the page (confidence low).

name: The Caaltu
summary: A civilisation that existed in Kahuturoa's time (Vastiri still forest, Vaal extant, Oriath recently founded, Ezomyr not yet struck by plague) and was only a memory by Maata's time. Little else is known.

name: Citizen Vanguard
summary: Force Kirac leads to defend Wraeclast against coming darkness; over 800 died against Sirus in Siege timeline.

name: Cultists of Kitava
summary: Followers of Kitava who plunder refugee ships fleeing Oriath, flood Oriath after its fall (Vilenta lets them into the Overseer's Tower) and hunt for food for their god; the drowned they leave behind wash ashore at the Twilight Strand.

sources.locator: Lilly: cultists have been plundering the refugee ships
Bannon: Kitava's cultists are constantly on the prowl seeking food for their god
Lani: Vilenta led the cultists into the Overseer's Tower

name: Druids of the Broken Circle
summary: Kalguuran nature-mystics under Medved, named after Olroth's gem use clouded their scrying.

alt_summaries.summary: Nature-mystics led by Medved; PoE2 names Gronel Starseer, Smalon Thickett, Avon Bruhn.
Kalguuran nature-mystic sect led by Medved, who could see the future by 'peering into the past'. Medved lost that sight the night Olroth set out alone with a gem.

name: Ebony Legion / Blackguards
summary: Dominus's Templar soldiers: Ebony Legion and Blackguards who enforce Oriath's rule and hunt in Wraeclast.

sources.locator: Lore: He also controls the Ebony Legion

name: The Elderslayers
summary: Group Zana assembled to hunt the Elder: Baran, Veritania, Drox, Al-Hezmin, led by Sirus. They became the Conquerors of the Atlas after going mad.

name: Eternal Empire
summary: Oriathan/imperial civilisation, also called the Sarn Empire, founded in 1 IC by Azmeri migrants under Tarcus Veruso on the ruins of the Vaal capital. Ruled by Emperors from Sarn, it held most of central Wraeclast with a Roman-style legion system until the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) destroyed it; Oriath survived as its successor.

chronology.relative: 1 IC to c. 1339 IC; roughly 260 years before PoE1 (1599-1600 IC)

sources.locator: lead paragraph and sections 'History' through 'The Cataclysm'
Act 1: Cemetery of the Eternals / Eternal prison areas

alt_summaries.summary: The Sarn-based Eternal Empire founded by Tarcus Veruso at 1 IC and ruled by Emperors from Sarn. The Cataclysm around 1339 IC ended it.
Old Empire of Wraeclast.

name: Exiles of Wraeclast
summary: Convicted Oriathans banished to Wraeclast; survive at Lioneye's Watch and later camps.

name: Ezomytes
summary: Clan people of Ezomyr, subjugated and enslaved by the Eternal Empire. Thane Rigwald rallied them in the Bloody Flowers Rebellion of 1333 IC and they joined the siege of Sarn.

alt_summaries.summary: People of Ezomyr and the Isles of Skothe who worship the First Ones; Ezomyr was later largely wiped by plague; speak Ezo.

name: Faridun
summary: Maraketh rejects (flawed or mutated newborns left in the dunes) raised by wandering Faridun tribes in the Vastiri, who accept necromancy and long for reunification with the akharas. In PoE2 Act 2 the Countess recruits them with the promise of resurrecting Jamanra.

sources.locator: Overview and Events in Path of Exile 2

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh outcasts left to die in the Vastiri, resentful and necromancy-dabbling; antagonists in PoE2 Act 2.
Desert people of Vastiri set against the Maraketh; featured in PoE2 as well.
Rejected Maraketh outcasts of the Vastiri desert, who ally with the Countess and resurrected Jamanra to feed the Beast.
Faridun sect led by Prince Azmadi, allied with the Serpent Clan avenging Keth's queen.

name: Gemling Legion
summary: Elite legions of the Eternal Empire created by Malachai: legionnaires infused with virtue gems, led by Captains, which gave the Empire military dominance. Chitus carried a master gem whose heartbeat bound every gemling to his own, so they fell when he died; survivors were transformed by the Cataclysm into the Undying.

name: The Godless Three
summary: Three thaumaturgists trained by Malachai: Shavronne of Umbra, Maligaro the Inquisitor and Doedre Darktongue. Maligaro and Doedre were burned by Voll; Malachai later revived all three to guard his heart, lungs and entrails.

alt_summaries.summary: Malachai's three most loyal servants: Maligaro, Shavronne, Doedre, guarding his organs.

name: House Azadi
summary: Trarthan Great House. Contract-assassin monopoly.

name: House Bardiya
summary: Trarthan Great House. Financiers; Merchant Council with greatest control today.

name: House Cyaxan
summary: Trarthan Great House. Drug trade, criminal syndicate and mass virtue gem implantation.

name: House Keita
summary: Trarthan Great House. Slave armies, flesh pits; failed to become a god; founded Korathin 872 IC.

name: The Immortal Syndicate
summary: Group of resurrected criminals and the missing forsaken masters under Catarina (the Mastermind), with 17 other members in four divisions (Transportation, Fortification, Research, Intervention); aims to become the ruling power in Wraeclast. Jun believes (not confirmed) the Horns of Kulamac give them their return-from-death ability.

name: Kalguuran settlers
summary: Runesmith people of Middengard who built Kingsmarch (Rog, Tujen, Dannig, Gwennen), led by the Cadigan kings; PoE1 Settlers of Kalguur continues into PoE2 Act 4.

alt_summaries.summary: People of Kalguur: rune-smiths who use runes of starlight, have no gods, lack inherent affinity for virtue gems, and live under King Cadigan; settlers in Wraeclast built Kingsmarch.
Seafaring Kalguuran, shown a gem image by Vaal survivors.

name: Karui
summary: Seafaring warrior people of the southern archipelago. Under King Kaom they allied with Voll's Purity Rebellion, took Lioneye's Watch and founded the first Karui settlement on the mainland; Kaom later fell at Highgate. The Empire had enslaved Karui under Chitus.

alt_summaries.summary: Nomadic seafaring people of Ngamakanui following the Karui Way; once peaceful farmers and fishermen until Tukohama armed them; ever-changing pantheon; Hinekora made the Halls of the Dead.
Island people of Ngamakanui.

Island people of Ngamakanui (Tukohama, Tasalio, Ngamahu, Tawhoa, Hinekora tribes) who in Act 4 ally with the Exile; ancestors remain in the Halls of the Dead and 'Ngakuramakoi' can be non-Karui by blood.
Island people who obstructed Doryani.

name: Arohongui tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Arohongui and is led by the chieftain Ikiaho; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Hinekora tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Hinekora and is led by the chieftain Tawhanuku; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Kitava tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Kitava and is led by the chieftain Utula; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Ngamahu tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Ngamahu and is led by the chieftain Kaom; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Ramako tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Ramako and is led by the chieftain Ahuana; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Rongokurai tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Rongokurai and is led by the chieftain Kahuturoa; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Tasalio tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tasalio and is led by the chieftain Rakiata; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Tawhoa tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tawhoa and is led by the chieftain Maata; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Tukohama tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tukohama and is led by the chieftain Akoya; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Valako tribe
summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Valako and is led by the chieftain Kiloava; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.

sources.locator: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

name: Keepers of the Flame (Order of the Purple Flame)
summary: Monastic order founded by Ailith after her visions of the Dreamer; they train in the Monastery to defend Wraeclast against the Hiveborn and tend the Genesis Tree. The PoE2 wiki calls it the Order of the Purple Flame; the Monk class belongs to it. It is a taboo among them to speak the Dreamer's true name (Chayula).

sources.locator: Visit the Monastery of the Keepers: "Welcome to our Monastery..."

alt_summaries.summary: Cult formed in Chayula's dreams, dedicated to destroying the Hiveborn; based at the Monastery of the Keepers.

name: Knights of the Sun
summary: Warriors and military enforcers under direct orders of the King, led by Olroth.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran martial order led by Olroth who adopted gems on weapons and armour.
Powerful Kalguuran warriors/enforcers directly under the King; led by Olroth; religious scrutiny by them drove some emigration.

name: The Lightless
summary: Necromantic army of possessed golems created by Kulemak, led by Abyssal Liches; ended the primeval civilisation.

name: The Maji
summary: Azmeri vanguard chosen when the Wildwood was made; they purge the Nameless and fight the King in the Mists, forbidden from touching virtue gems ('Tears of the Maji').

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri vanguard sent into the Wildwood to wait while it is purged of evil, waging war on the King in the Mists.

name: Maraketh
summary: Desert people of the Vastiri led by Sekhemas, living in akhara (tribes). In 1333 IC Sekhema Deshret joined the Purity Rebellion in exchange for the return of the Vastiri Plains; later, Deshret sealed the Highgate mines. A large tribe lives at Highgate in PoE1; the Ardura akhara and Sekhema Asala appear in PoE2.

alt_summaries.summary: Matriarchal people led by sekhema, ancient dwellers of Vastiri for 304 generations; endured the Winter of the World, expelled the Lightless, had a thousand-year golden age at Keth, then lost their gods to the Beast's slumber and drifted into the desert.
Desert nomads of the Vastiri.
Desert people of the Vastiri; the Ardura akhara and the honoured dead of Deshar are Maraketh.

name: Meridian Free Traders
summary: Trade guild that sent Raulf to assist executing the Kingsmarch charter; in PoE2 it controls boat charters (Makoru captains the Aurora May under it).

alt_summaries.summary: Kingsmarch guild under which Makoru's Aurora May works; requires an account and charter from Rog.

name: Mutewind (warband)
summary: One of the three Warbands in Warbands league, alongside Brinerot and Redblades; the wiki calls them the Peak-dwellers. Their outcast Qianga delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay for the Order of the Djinn. Mutewind Warbands also appear as bosses in the Delve map Frozen Hollow.

sources.locator: Warbands item list: Mutewind Wildrunner, Mutewind Lynx, Mutewind Seal
Qianga entry: 'a Mutewind warband outcast'; 'The Mutewind|Peak-dwellers'

name: House Grattus (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'Grattus Signet'.

name: House Nevalius (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'Nevalius Inheritance'.

name: House Perandus (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Perandus Pact'.

name: House Phrecia (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Hand of Phrecia'.

name: House Veruso (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'Veruso's Ambition'.

name: Priests of the Chalice
summary: Religious order that read the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran priesthood led by Uhtred; found the ancient artefact at the shrine.
Kalguuran priesthood (Priests of the Chalice) that interpreted the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes; Uhtred was its High Priest.

name: Order of the Djinn
summary: Secret society founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper (Ahkeli) that protects Wraeclast from calamity and guards dangerous artefacts (Forbidden Vaults near the Oasis, Act 9); takes one orphan from each culture. Members forged and delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay (video). Janus Perandus's betrayal let Catarina raid the vault and the Order was slain except Jun and Janus; in PoE2 Jun is rebuilding it. Past members include Ixchel (later the Trialmaster).

sources.locator: 1:07 order of the Djinn; 16:34 Starforge; 20:10 infiltration of Forbidden Vault

alt_summaries.summary: Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamity and guard dangerous artefacts. Icius Perandus and, much later, Janus Perandus belonged to it.
Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamities; Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.

Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper that guards dangerous artefacts and prevents calamities; selects one orphan from each culture. Members include Jun, Janus Perandus, Saresh, Ixchel, Dhunan, Sumei (investigated Kalandra's duplication of artefacts). Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.
Secret order (Jado's) replenishing its ranks; Jado confirms they infiltrated the Sel Khari and will be in Oriath.
Secret order founded by the Maraketh to guard relics and protect Wraeclast; nearly destroyed by Janus's betrayal in PoE1's Betrayal; Jun rebuilds it in secret, per PoE2.

name: The Pale Council
summary: Group of four Pale Court bosses (Yriel, Eber, Volkuur and Inya) fought through the Prophecy system; the wiki says the Pale Council fight no longer exists after 3.17.0. In the wiki's in-world history the Pale Council were rulers of an unidentified people, likely the Karui.

sources.locator: section 'The Pale Council': '[[The Pale Council]] is a group comprising of Yriel, the Feral Lord, Eber, the Plaguemaw, Volkuur, and Inya'
Drops: 'sequence of last alive member of the Pale Council is random'; Version history 3.0.0 'The Pale Council encounter has been rebalanced'
Header: 'The Pale Council fight no longer exists in Path of Exile'

name: Perandus family
summary: Wealthiest merchant-lender family of the Eternal Empire (motto 'With piety and justice'). Blocked from the throne by the Phrecians, they rigged Izaro's Labyrinth so Chitus Perandus won; Cadiro looted the treasury before the fall. Descendants include Syndicate member Janus Perandus.

sources.locator: forum announcement describing Cadiro's stolen treasury and indebted dead

alt_summaries.summary: Wealthy and powerful Eternal Empire family that put Malachai in place; basis for the Perandus league treasures.

name: Phrecian dynasty
summary: Unbroken line of emperors descended from Alano Phrecia, who founded the line after killing the 'dark being' in 35 IC. It ran from Alano through Romira and Tyndarus to Izaro, who was childless.

sources.locator: sections 'Reign of Alano Phrecia' to 'Reign of Izaro'

name: Precursors
summary: Technologically superior ancient civilisation that wholly predates the Winter of the World; mastered corruption, built the Towers (terraforming), the Precursor Weapon and the Arbiter of Ash, then triggered cataclysms of fire, eruptions and sky-impacts. Pictographs read 'Death lies within'.

chronology.relative: further before the Vaal than the Vaal are before the present

name: Primeval Civilization ("Proto-Vaal")
summary: Ancient civilisation preceding the Vaal, unearthed in the Azurite Mine; the name "Proto-Vaal" is an internal term never used in-game and no link to the Vaal is established.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient culture (internally called 'Proto-Vaal') buried beneath Vaal and Lightless ruins in the Azurite Mines, known from glyphs; First King Uzaza, tyrant Putembo, last king Aul. No proven link to the Vaal.

name: Purity Rebellion
summary: Coalition led by High Templar Voll of Thebrus against Chitus' gem-and-thaumaturgy 'thaumatocracy'. Its supporters included Victario, Ondar, Geofri, Kastov and Adus, with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh allies.

name: Redblades
summary: Human tribe descended from those who settled the Titans' volcanoes; they ritually sacrifice humans to the Molten One, possibly because a Titan destroyed an outpost of El'Abin.

name: Remembrancers
summary: Kalguuran scribes who documented the explorations; the Prime Remembrancer's logbooks tell the expedition's fall.

alt_summaries.summary: Documentarians of Kalguuran explorations.

name: Runefathers
summary: Aldur's chosen apprentices and artisans of runesmithing; forged the Triskelion Flame to reunite fractured Middengard.

sources.locator: ===The Triskelion Flame===: "After Aldur had passed away, the Runefathers gathered to forge the Triskelion Flame."

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran runesmiths who gathered after Aldur's death to forge the Triskelion Flame in his honour.

name: Karui Slave Rebellion
summary: Rebellion of enslaved Karui in Oriath led by Utula.

name: Order of the Templar
summary: Theocratic order led by a High Templar that worships Innocence. Within the Eternal Empire it produced figures such as High Templars Andronicus and Voll; after the Cataclysm it governed the unaffected island of Oriath as the Templar Theocracy, with Dominus and Avarius as its PoE1-era High Templars.

alt_summaries.summary: A human faction led by a High Templar, governing the theocracy of Oriath in the name of Innocence. Its members include High Templars Dominus, Voll and Avarius.
Theocratic order ruling Oriath.

name: The Crimson Scribe
summary: Society named as the client on Heist contracts targeting the Seal of Solaris, Seal of Lunaris, Ez Myrae Tome, Staff of the First Sin Eater and Golden Ibis; its targets indicate interest in the Winter of the World and the primeval civilization.

name: The Ring
summary: Rogue guild that runs the Rogue Harbour and fulfils Heist contracts for clients such as Administrator Qotra and the Crimson Scribe. The Count Geonor passage in the wiki says he contracted the Ring. Its leader is referred to only as 'the Boss'.

name: The Unblinking Eye
summary: Mysterious group associated with the Templars involved in notable events in Wraeclast's history.

name: The Three Sisters
summary: Cross-cultural myth of the sun, moon and earth sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and ended the Winter of the World; named differently by Eternals, Maraketh, Karui, Azmeri and the Wildwood Draiocht (Catha, Mhacha, Morrigan).

alt_summaries.summary: Sun, Moon (and Earth) sisters/gods named differently per culture who ended the Winter of the World by destroying Kulemak's mortal form. Minimal node; owned by another domain.

name: Trarthans
summary: People of Trarthus descended from Eternal Empire exiles and slaves, led by four Great Houses.

name: The Vaal
summary: Oldest identified civilisation of Wraeclast and in its heyday its most powerful nation; first known users of virtue gems, practitioners of mass blood sacrifice and slavery. All but 3,126 died in the Vaal Cataclysm; survivors assimilated into the Azmeri.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient Vaal civilisation.
Vaal civilisation of Utzaal and its remnants; Alva is a descendant of Vaal survivors.

name: The Royal Architects of Atzoatl
summary: Group of Vaal architects serving Atziri who built the Temple; Incursion has Vaal Architect mini-bosses. PoE2 Medallion flavour names Architects of the Guild, Vault, Destruction, Hoard, Forge and Nexus and associates Quipolatl, Puhuarte, Juatalotli, Hayoxi, Estazunti with them.

name: Vaal survivors / Savage tribes heirs
summary: The 3,126 survivors who merged into Azmeri tribes; later Azmeri/Karui cultures inherit Vaal remnants. Descendants of Vaal blood persist (e.g. Alva Valai; the Cuachic).

sources.locator: Doryani: 'a living descendant of our people'

name: Vox family
summary: Oriathan nobility that became a criminal enterprise; the wiki describes the twins Vic and Vinny Vox using coercion, blackmail and violence to hold a place at the centre of Oriath business and social life. Descended from Cardinal Sanctus Vox.

name: Warbands (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind)
summary: Three roaming warring clans of Warbands league (2.0.0) with leaders and elites: Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind; members Korell Goya, Guff Grenn, Rin Yuushu later joined the Syndicate.

name: Watchers of Decay
summary: Ancient organisation of parents founded when a nameless god told an Azmeri mother whose child was stolen about the Elder. They forged Starforge to subdue it by separating form and spirit. Their Map Device (Book of Memories p9) later became the Atlas device. Associated with the Order of the Djinn on the wiki; membership of Egrin/Qianga/Betucia is unclear.

name: Abyss league
summary: Abyss league Launched 2017-12-08 (version 3.1.0). Abysses are cracks and pits spawning monsters; introduces abyss jewels, Stygian Vises, Abyssal Depths and Abyssal Liches.

name: Affliction league
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.23.0 (8 Dec 2023 - 26 Mar 2024): the player cleanses the Affliction of the Viridian Wildwood with sacred wisps, trains with the Azmeri and unlocks Wildwood ascendancy classes; the King in the Mists is the antagonist.

name: Allflame league (Curse of the Allflame)
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.29.0 (24 Jul 2026; announced end 9 Nov 2026): aboard Valerie's ship the Sovereign, Exiles chart the Fathomless Depths with Allflame lanterns and craft with Vesper.

name: Ambush league
summary: Ambush league launched 2014-03-05 (1.1.0, Sacrifice of the Vaal); introduced Strongboxes. Ran with hardcore Invasion league.

name: Anarchy league
summary: Anarchy league launched 2013-06-07 (0.11.0); introduced rogue exiles and league challenges. Hardcore twin: Onslaught.

name: Ancestor league (Trial of the Ancestors)
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.22.0 (18 Aug - 5 Dec 2023): Exiles use Silver Coins to enter the Karui afterlife and field a team of Karui warriors in the Trial of the Ancestors tournament against fallen chieftains, under Hinekora.

name: Archnemesis league
summary: Challenge league in which petrified monsters are imbued with itemised Archnemesis modifiers to build custom rare boss fights. Mechanics-driven; no dedicated narrative NPC in the wiki corpus.

name: Bestiary league
summary: Bestiary league Launched 2018-03-02 (version 3.2.0). Einhar Frey teaches the Exile to capture beasts with nets, for beastcrafting and to challenge the Spirit Beasts (the First Ones).

name: Betrayal league
summary: Betrayal league Launched 2018-12-07 (version 3.5.0). Jun Ortoi leads the hunt for the Immortal Syndicate, which has taken the forsaken masters; revamps the master system.

name: Beyond league
summary: Beyond league launched 2014-08-20 (1.2.0, Forsaken Masters): extradimensional demons invade via portals that grow with nearby kills, culminating in a unique boss. Hardcore twin of Rampage.

name: Blight league
summary: Challenge league in which Sister Cassia asks the exile to defend a Purification Pump against fungal Blight growths; rewards Oils used to Anoint items.

name: Bloodlines league
summary: Bloodlines league Launched 2014-12-13 (version 1.3.0). Hardcore twin of Torment; Bloodline-empowered monsters with special modifiers. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

name: Breach league
summary: Breach league Launched 2016-12-02 (version 2.5.0). Breaches open parallel realms of otherworldly monsters; splinters form Breachstones to challenge the five Breachlords in their domains.

name: Crucible league
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.21.0 (7 Apr - 15 Aug 2023, 'Path of Exile: Crucible'): Crucible Forges grant equipment a passive tree, and Primeval Remnants open portals to the Forge of the Titans.

name: Delirium league
summary: Challenge league in which Mirrors of Delirium in each area release a spreading fog of madness; leads to the Simulacrum and Cluster Jewels.

name: Delve league
summary: Delve league Launched 2018-08-31 (version 3.4.0). Niko the Mad guides the Exile into the infinite Azurite Mine beneath Wraeclast, powered by Voltaxic Sulphite.

name: Domination league
summary: Domination league launched 2013-10-23 (1.0.0, Path of Exile release); introduced Shrines. Hardcore twin: Nemesis.

name: Echoes of the Atlas (3.13.0)
summary: League/expansion that introduced the Maven and the Envoy.

name: Essence league
summary: Essence league launched 2016-09-02 (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds): frozen monsters hold an Essence; freeing them grants it. Essences give guaranteed affixes and can be corrupted.

name: Expedition league
summary: Challenge league introducing four Kalguuran expedition NPCs (Gwennen, Tujen, Rog, Dannig) who excavate the lost settlements of their ancestors with explosives. The Kalguur are referenced again in Settlers (Kingsmarch) and in PoE2.

name: Harbinger league
summary: Harbinger league launched 2017-08-04 (3.0.0, The Fall of Oriath): otherworldly Harbingers, defeated by destroying their minions, drop shards of currency.

name: Harvest league
summary: Challenge league in which the Azmeri outcast Oshabi has the exile plant seeds in the Sacred Grove and harvest Lifeforce for crafting; ends with the Avatar of the Grove boss. Later reworked into a core mechanic.

name: Heist league
summary: Challenge league in which the exile uses Rogue's Markers to enter the Rogue Harbour, run Contracts for the Ring, and hire rogues to steal valuables from fortified caches (Contracts, Blueprints, Grand Heists).

name: Incursion league
summary: PoE1 3.3.0 challenge league (June 2018) in which Alva Valai opens incursions 2,000 years into the past to the Temple of Atzoatl; later became a core Master mechanic.

name: Invasion league
summary: Invasion league Launched 2014-03-05 (version 1.1.0). Hardcore twin of Ambush; invasion bosses spawn in areas. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

name: Lake of Kalandra league
aliases: Path of Exile: Lake of Kalandra
summary: Challenge league in which the player assembles a Mirrored Tablet of reflected encounters and enters the Lake of Kalandra, meeting the ancient trapped entity Kalandra.

chronology.relative: 3.19.0 'Path of Exile: Lake of Kalandra', 2022-08-19 to 2022-12-06

alt_summaries.summary: Challenge league released 19 Aug 2022 in version 3.19.0 (ended 6 Dec 2022): Mirrored Tablets let players build reflected encounters in the Lake of Kalandra.

name: Keepers of the Flame league
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.27.0 (31 Oct 2025 - 2 Mar 2026): the Exile works with Ailith to repel Hiveborn invading via stabilised Breach connections and grows the Genesis Tree; Breach joined the core game in 3.28.0.

sources.locator: lead; Into the Breach version history

alt_summaries.summary: PoE1 league (3.27.0) that introduced the new Breach (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree); the mechanic became core in 3.28.0 replacing the original Breach. Minimal node; full release data owned by another domain.

name: Legion league
summary: Legion league Launched 2019-06-07 (version 3.7.0). Timeless Monoliths reveal legions frozen mid-battle; Emblems open the Domain of Timeless Conflict. Legion mechanic reworked in 3.29 per wiki (incubators no longer drop).

name: Mercenaries league (Mercenaries of Trarthus)
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.26.0 (13 Jun - 27 Oct 2025): lawless Trarthan veterans can be fought and hired; noble mercenaries descend from the four death-trade Great Houses.

name: Metamorph league
summary: Challenge league in which the alchemist Tane Octavius has the exile gather organs from monsters to build shape-changing Metamorphs; introduces Catalysts.

name: Mirage league
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.28.0 (6 Mar 2026; scheduled to end 20 Jul 2026): with Sekhema Varashta the Exile frees djinn tortured by the Afarud via mirages and the astral realm; endgame necromancer Saresh.

name: Necro Settlers event
summary: Event run Nov 2024 - Feb 2025 during the extended Settlers league, combining Necropolis content with Settlers.

sources.locator: intro: 'Necro Settlers event was held from November 2024 to February 2025'

name: Necropolis league
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.24.0 (29 Mar - 23 Jul 2024): Undertaker Arimor lends the Exile his Lantern to haunt monsters, collect their corpses and bury them in the Necropolis for grave crafting; Embers of the Allflame transform monsters.

name: Nemesis league
summary: Nemesis league launched 2013-10-23 (1.0.0); every rare monster has a Nemesis modifier. Standard twin: Domination.

name: Onslaught league
summary: Onslaught league launched 2013-06-07 (0.11.0); monsters have 20% increased movement and attack speed. Standard twin: Anarchy.

name: Perandus league
summary: Perandus league launched 2016-03-04 (2.2.0, Ascendancy): after the Cataclysm Cadiro Perandus hid family treasures in caches across Wraeclast; players open guarded caches and trade Perandus Coins with Cadiro.

name: Legacy of Phrecia
summary: 'Legacy of Phrecia': a limited returning PoE1 event (ascendancy/idol rework). First run ended 23 Apr 2025; it returned during the 3.27 (Keepers of the Flame) cycle from 29 Jan 2026 for about 20 days, per third-party news. Its lore link to the ancient Phrecian/imperial-heartland history is by name only (unverified).

chronology.relative: first run ended Apr 2025; 3.27-cycle rerun 29 Jan - 19 Feb 2026 (third-party news)

sources.locator: article on the end of the event (23 Apr 2025)
official event page (not re-fetched by checker)

alt_summaries.summary: Event (run after the Necro Settlers event until 23 April 2025, with a second run later adding random modifiers) that replaces the 19 ascendancy classes with alternate 'whacky ideas' classes and replaces the Atlas passive tree with an idol system.

name: Prophecy league
summary: Prophecy league launched 2016-06-03 (2.3.0): silver coins traded with Navali for prophecies; the Pale Council league bosses of the Pale Court were tied to prophecies.

name: Rampage league
summary: Rampage league Launched 2014-08-20 (version 1.2.0). Kill-streak mechanic (paired with Beyond), part of Forsaken Masters. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

name: Ritual league
summary: Challenge league in which a Ritual Altar in each zone starts a wave fight that awards Tribute, spendable on a shop of pre-identified items. Narrative content is minimal in PoE1; the same Ritual altar mechanic returns in PoE2's Forbidden Rites league (0.5.5).

name: Sacrifice of the Vaal
summary: PoE1 1.1.0 mini-expansion centred on Atziri and Vaal side areas.

name: Sanctum league (The Forbidden Sanctum)
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.20.0 (9 Dec 2022 - 4 Apr 2023; shipped as 'Path of Exile: The Forbidden Sanctum'): a roguelite run through an ancient Templar enclave beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, controlled by a malevolent entity (Lycia is its fourth-floor boss).

name: Scourge league
summary: Challenge league in which The Last to Die gives the exile a Blood Crucible to corrupt items while fighting through a demon-ridden 'Nightmare' mirror of Wraeclast; its monsters became the new Beyond monsters.

name: Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas
summary: PoE1 expansion 3.26.0 (13 Jun 2025) containing Mercenaries league and the Originator endgame storyline (Zana the Originator, Eagon Caeserius, Threads of the Originator); Settlers' Kingsmarch services were added to the core game.

sources.locator: release 2025-06-13, 'Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas' 3.26.0

alt_summaries.summary: Expansion launched 13 June 2025 (3.26.0, with Mercenaries league) adding Eagon, Zana the Originator, Memory Tears and the Incarnations; 3.28.0 reworked the Atlas.

name: Sentinel league
summary: Challenge league in which Sentinel drones empower monsters; Power Cores charge Sentinel filaments and Recombinators combine two equipment items. Sentinel mechanics were added to the core game in 3.25; existing Recombinators remained usable.

name: Settlers of Kalguur league
summary: PoE1 expansion/league 3.25.0 (26 Jul 2024; league ended 9 Jun 2025 22:00 UTC / 10 Jun 2025 00:00 GMT+2 per GGG after multiple extensions for PoE2 Early Access, over 45 weeks): the Exile helps Kalguuran settlers build Kingsmarch, a harbour meant to facilitate trade between the settlers, the Karui archipelago and Kalguur. Town-building ended in 3.26.0; Kingsmarch services joined the core game.

sources.locator: GGG forum "What Will Happen When The Settlers League Ends": "The league will end on Jun 10, 2025 12:00 AM (GMT+2)"; "Kingsmarch will be going core in 3.26"

name: Siege of the Atlas (3.17.0)
summary: Expansion that added the Searing Exarch, Eater of Worlds and the Eldritch system.

name: Synthesis league
summary: Challenge league in which fragments of lost memories are scattered through Wraeclast; the player stabilises them and links them in the Memory Nexus. Guide NPC Cavas turns out to be the High Templar Venarius. Not added to the core game; its bosses (Synthetes, Venarius) survive as unique maps.

alt_summaries.summary: 3.6.0 challenge league (Mar 2019) centred on Cavas and decaying memories; bosses later became unique map content and Kirac missions.

name: Talisman league
summary: Talisman league launched 2015-12-11 (version 2.1.0). Monsters are possessed by ancient Ezomyte Talismans; killing them yields the Talisman. Boss: Rigwald, the Wolven King.

name: Tempest league
summary: Tempest league launched 2015-07-10 (2.0.0, The Awakening); hardcore sibling of Warbands that introduced Tempests, area modifiers that alter monsters and players (size, damage, drops).

name: Torment league
summary: Torment league launched 2014-12-13 (1.3.0): spirits of tormented criminals haunt areas, flee when met, imbue monsters and yield their ill-gotten gains when slain. Hardcore twin: Bloodlines.

name: Ultimatum league
summary: Vaal-themed challenge league in which the Trialmaster, servant of the entity Chaos, offers escalating Trials of Chaos for the player to risk or bank rewards. Re-integrated into the core game in 3.23.0.

name: Warbands league
summary: Warbands league Launched 2015-07-10 (version 2.0.0). Warring clans (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind) roam Wraeclast in synergistic groups with leaders and elites. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

name: Absence of Mercy and Empathy
summary: The Maven's realm in the Atlas; entering it with a The Maven's Writ starts The Maven's Game epilogue quest and hosts the Maven pinnacle fight.

sources.locator: intro paragraph: 'This quest will automatically be obtained after entering Absence of Mercy and Empathy using a The Maven's Writ'

name: Absence of Patience and Wisdom
summary: Atlas map realm where The Searing Exarch is fought in the Searing Exarch epilogue quest.

sources.locator: Quest log: 'Enter The Absence of Patience and Wisdom'

name: Absence of Symmetry and Harmony
summary: Atlas map realm where The Eater of Worlds is fought in the Eater of Worlds epilogue quest.

sources.locator: Quest log: 'Enter Absence of Symmetry and Harmony'

name: Absence of Value and Meaning
summary: Elder's arena in the Atlas.

sources.locator: 'defeat The Elder in Absence of Value and Meaning'

name: Abyssal Depths
summary: Areas reached from Abysses containing Abyssal monsters and lich bosses Amanamu and Ulaman.

name: Abyssal Depths (Delve)
summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) that uses Abyss theme and contains Abyss monsters. It is distinct from the Abyssal City biome (which spawns The Lich's Tomb) and from the Abyssal Depths map area (existing node loc_abyssal_depths).

sources.locator: Intro: 'Abyssal Depths is a biome within the Azurite Mine'; hatnote: 'For the area accessible from completing an Abyss encounter in map'; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'

name: The Alluring Abyss
summary: PoE1 area for Uber Atziri (Mortal fragments).

name: The Ancient Pyramid (PoE1 Act 2)
summary: Vaal pyramid in Act 2 housing the Dark Altar where the Vaal Oversoul is fought.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal pyramid in the Caverns beyond the Vaal Ruins with the Dark Altar.

name: The Apex of Sacrifice
summary: PoE1 map-device area (Sacrifice fragments) in which Atziri is fought.

name: Atlas of Worlds
summary: The dreamlike plane of interlinked worlds at the centre of PoE1's endgame; its mists reflect the desires of whoever walks it (Veritania's journal). Time there is 'a mirage' (Baran). Reached via the Map Device.

sources.locator: Journal I: 'There is only my will, my thoughts, and my expectations, reflected as countless echoes'
Journal III: 'Time in the Atlas is a mirage'

name: Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal)
summary: Past version of the temple unlocked via Ancient Beacons; the present ruin is the Lost Temple. Built via the Temple Console; Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal after Act 3/4.

sources.locator: lead; Ancient Beacon; Doryani will activate the time portal

name: Aul's Domain (Crystal King's Throne)
summary: Delve area (internally 'Proto-Vaal city') of the Azurite Mine where the crystal-encased citadel and throne of Aul, the Crystal King, lie.

sources.locator: Primeval civilization; footnote: 'Proto-Vaal' is the internal name of Delve's Primeval Chamber and The Crystal King's Throne

alt_summaries.summary: Delve node (Primeval Ruins biome) containing the Primeval Citadel where Aul is fought.

name: Axiom Prison
summary: Ancient clifftop prison (no one remembers who built it) used by every power that ruled Wraeclast; its warden Brutus was mutated; Act 1 area from Lower Prison to Warden's Chambers.

sources.locator: Shavronne in her tower in the Prison

alt_summaries.summary: Eternal outpost warded by Brutus where Shavronne of Umbra experimented on him; blocked Karui advance.
Prison complex reached through the Act 6 Ridge; contains Shavronne's Tower, where Shavronne's spirit is killed for Sin.

name: Azala Vaal
summary: Vaal capital named after the burning of Lira Vaal's temple; now buried beneath Sarn where the Azmeri founded the Eternal Empire's capital.

alt_summaries.summary: Former capital of the Vaal Empire; Tarcus Veruso planted his banner here to found Sarn and the Eternal Empire.

name: Viridian Wildwood
summary: Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons there, the Maji fight the Nameless and the King in the Mists. PoE2 Last of the Druids setting.

sources.locator: The Winter of the World > The Viridian Wildwood
paragraph on the forest not existing until 3.23.0

alt_summaries.summary: Haven created by the Draiocht as refuge from the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons; haunted by shadowy creatures such as the King in the Mists; home of the Maji.

Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World, where time loops in seasons. Contested by the Nameless and the King in the Mists; Chaos believes the forest did not exist until the 3.23 timeline.
Wildwood encounter on the Atlas, connected to Sacred Bloom rewards; Aoife is bound here.

name: Azmerian Ranges
summary: Mountain homeland of the ancient Azmeri; origin of the migrants who founded Sarn and the Eternal Empire, and where the Vaal first met the Azmeri.

name: The Azurite Mine
summary: Infinitely scaling dungeon beneath Wraeclast reached from the Mine Encampment; contains Primeval ruins, Vaal city, abyssal city biomes and darkness.

name: The Belly of the Beast
summary: Interior of the Beast with the Black Core.

name: The Brine King's Reef
summary: Blood-reef boss area at the end of Act 6, reached by Weylam Roth's ship the Black Crest, summoned with the Black Flag at the Beacon.

name: The Cathedral Rooftop (Act 10)
summary: Rooftop where Bannon holds off Kitava's cultists.

alt_summaries.summary: Where the Sign of Purity is used against Kitava.

name: Chamber of Innocence
summary: Templar chamber in Oriath built under High Templar Avarius whose stained glass windows tell the Sin and Innocence story.

alt_summaries.summary: Chamber where Avarius becomes Innocence.

name: Chamber of Sins
summary: Laboratory built by Chitus where Maligaro conducted flesh experiments, opposed by nearby Phrecia Cathedral; named by Archbishop Geofri.

alt_summaries.summary: Old Empire site where Maligaro worked; holds the Baleful Gem.
Inquisitor Maligaro's laboratory in Phrecia, with a secret passage to the Den.

name: The Control Blocks
summary: Templar prison blocks in Oriath.

name: The Crystal Veins
summary: Highgate caverns holding the Rapture Device, which the exile reactivates to enter the Beast.

alt_summaries.summary: Cave where the Rapture Device stands.

name: Mines (Delve)
summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) that generates only at the top levels of the mine; contains Metallic, Serrated, Pristine and Aetheric fossils. Introduced in 3.4.0.

sources.locator: Intro: 'Mines is one of the biomes of the Azurite Mine. It only generates at the very top levels of the mine'; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game'

name: Doedre's Cesspool
summary: Sewer area of the Toxic Conduits in Sarn where Doedre is killed in the Cauldron.

sources.locator: Doedre's Cesspool contains The Cauldron boss arena

name: Domain of Timeless Conflict
summary: Area opened by combining Emblems in the map device; heart of the timeless conflict between legions.

name: The Ebony Barracks
summary: Blackguard base across the river in Sarn.

name: Eternal Laboratory
summary: Malachai's laboratory of the Eternal Empire, built on the archbishop Lazhwar's thaumaturgy research into maps; Zana's hideout alternative in the legacy Atlas quests.

sources.locator: Eternal Empire section: 'Lazhwar... discovered maps to create the Eternal Laboratory'
Assignment: 'Talk to Zana in your Hideout or the Eternal Laboratory'

name: Eye of Hinekora / Halls of the Dead
summary: Karui afterlife realm unlocked by rescuing Matiki: Tests of Mettle for Kaom, Maata and Rakiata, the Halls of the Dead with Yama's trial and the audience with Hinekora.

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 Act 4 area accessible after rescuing Matiki; gateway to the Halls of the Dead and Trial of the Ancestors.

name: Ezomyr
summary: Ezomyte homeland on a landmass west of the Wraeclastian mainland (with the Isles of Skothe), later largely wiped out by a plague; Ogham forests in PoE2 Act 1.

name: The Fathomless Depths
summary: Underwater endgame area explored via a Bathysphere and Allflame lanterns; a pit of deathly light lies below.

name: Fellshrine Ruins
summary: Ruined former Freesia Cathedral area of Wraeclast, above the Forbidden Sanctum; Eramir calls the Fellshrine a shadow of what was once good in Wraeclast.

name: The Forbidden Sanctum
summary: Ancient Templar enclave/ossuary-library beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, four floors deep, abandoned for a long time and now controlled by Lycia, who lures treasure hunters in through portals; floors shift from tidy library to Scourge-infested crypt.

sources.locator: '==Lore==': 'ancient Templar enclave hidden beneath the Fellshrine Ruins'
[4:05]-[4:30] four floors, library to crypt; [10:35]-[11:30] ossuary and pact

alt_summaries.summary: Templar catacombs under the Fellshrine Ruins (PoE1 Sanctum): lithomancy, necromancy and hidden truths of Innocence's ascension. Background for Oriathan Templar secrecy; no source ties it to the Twilight Order.

name: The Forest Encampment
summary: Former Azmeri/exile village taken over by Ralakesh through Greust; located between the Ashen Fields and the Northern Forest in Act 7.

sources.locator: Ralakesh is located in The Forest Encampment

alt_summaries.summary: Act 2 town in the Phrecian forest, a village of Greust, Silk, Yeena, Eramir.

name: Forge of the Titans
summary: Primeval forge reached through Primeval Remnants during Crucible league, where equipment trees are combined; the stone body and voice of the Molten One, the last known Titan, can be met there.

sources.locator: '==League Mechanic==' Primeval Remnant / Forge of the Titans
Molten One entry: 'During Crucible league, his stone body and voice can be encountered in the Forge of the Titans'

alt_summaries.summary: Volcanic caldera (Crucible league) where the Molten One dwells and the Redblades worship him.

name: The Grand Architect's Temple
summary: Delve node in the Vaal Outpost biome housing the boss Ahuatotli, the Blind.

name: The Halls of the Dead
summary: Karui afterlife created by Hinekora before the Slumbering of the Gods as a place for Karui souls; where fallen chieftains reside and the Trial of the Ancestors is held.

sources.locator: '==Items==' (portal to the Halls of the Dead)

name: The High Gardens
summary: Act 8 gardens associated with Izaro, where Yugul lurks.

name: Highgate
summary: Mountain region where Veruso buried the virtue gems ('Tears of Maji'), where slaves mined them under Chitus, where Malachai placed the Rapture Device and the Beast lies beneath, and where a Maraketh tribe lives in PoE1.

sources.locator: 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Slave trade', 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh-held mining settlement north of Sarn, Act 4 town.
Mining town built over the Beast's corpse; Act 9 town whose waters run red with the Beast's blood. Maraketh Irasha, Tasuni and relic hunters Petarus and Vanja live here.

name: Isles of Skothe
summary: Landmass west of Sarn named with Ezomyr as the origin of the Ezomytes.

name: Kalguur
summary: Homeland of the Kalguur people in Middengard, a distant continent southeast/east of Wraeclast; not directly accessible but referenced by Expedition and Settlers of Kalguur.

alt_summaries.summary: Homeland of the Kalguurans on the continent Middengard, south-east of Wraeclast; ruled by a mysterious King Cadigan who gives charters to successful outposts.

name: Kaom's Stronghold
summary: Karui stronghold within the Beast where Kaom is fought.

name: The Karui Fortress
summary: Act 6 area containing Tukohama's Keep, where the Karui war god is fought.

name: Karui Shores
summary: Epilogue hub leading to the Atlas of Worlds.

sources.locator: Upon entering Karui Shores talk to Helena

name: Keth
summary: Ancient Maraketh city and trade empire at the meeting of seven rivers, called the 'glory of the world'; ruins form an Act 2 area in PoE2.

sources.locator: Walkthrough 'Use the Desert Map to travel to Keth'

alt_summaries.summary: Buried city where the Water Goddess Halani lies and the Essence of Water is found.

name: Kingsmarch
summary: Kalguuran harbour town on Ngamakanui, hub of Act 4 where the Exile hires the Aurora May. Founded in PoE1's Settlers of Kalguur; Tujen says they first picked the spot to stash supplies and 'now it's going to be a city'. In the epilogue its ruins are revisited by Dannig and Makoru.

sources.locator: intro + '==NPCs=='; Trivia 'Act 4 town in Path of Exile 2'

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran-chartered port and hub town on the Karui coast, reached via Johan in the Karui Shores (Epilogue). Run by the King's Hand under a Charter, it hosts Dannig, Tujen, Rog, Isla, Faustus, Raulf and Sonja. In PoE2 it is the Act 4 town and later lies in ruins in the endgame.

name: Korathin
summary: Capital of Trarthus, declared by Ixan Keita in 872 IC and built by his slaves.

name: Lake of Kalandra
summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars in primordial Wraeclast where Kalandra is trapped. The league version was a mirror-realm assembled from a Mirrored Tablet and was not added to the core game.

sources.locator: League Mechanic and note on core game

alt_summaries.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars that existed when 'nothing but the lake' did; Kalandra is trapped in it. The Kalandra league lets the Exile stage reflected encounters there.

name: The Lich's Tomb
summary: Delve node of the Azurite Mine, found in the Abyssal City biome at depth 90+; it always contains the boss fight with Kurgal, the Blackblooded in the Abyssal Sanctum. The boss room is no longer accessible in a new instance after the kill.

sources.locator: Intro: 'It can only appeared in 90+ depths in the Abyssal City biome ... it always contains the boss fight with Kurgal, the Blackblooded'; 'After the boss fight has been finished, the node can be revisited'

name: Lioneye's Watch
summary: Southern Eternal garrison commanded by General Marceus Lioneye, taken by Kaom's Karui in the Purity Rebellion; later the survivors' town in PoE1 Acts 1 and 6.

sources.locator: Lioneye's Watch is the Act 6 town

alt_summaries.summary: Act 1 town of exile survivors on the coast, named after General Marceus Lioneye; conquered by Kaom's Karui in the past.
Coastal refugee town on the Twilight Strand; Act 1 town and, in Part Two, the Act 6 town where Tarkleigh, Bestel, Lilly Roth and Sin await the exile.

name: Lira Vaal / Atziri's Temple
summary: Royal temple of Atziri and Vaal capital for much of its history; rebuilt by Xipocado and Doryani as a self-reconstructing marvel. PoE2 Fate of the Vaal league lets players modify its layout.

name: The Lord's Labyrinth
summary: A labyrinth built by Emperor Izaro in 1317 IC as a test to choose his successor, opened on the second Galvano of Azmeri. Chitus won it by betraying Weylin, and later sealed Izaro inside. In PoE1 it is the Act 1 quest that leads to the Trials of Ascendancy.

sources.locator: section 'Reign of Izaro' and 'The Lord's Labyrinth'

alt_summaries.summary: Trap-filled maze built by Emperor Izaro in Sarn to pick his successor, opened 1317 IC. Chitus won it; the exile later challenges it to earn ascendancy points.

name: The Lunaris Temple
summary: Temple on west side of Sarn, Piety's laboratory filled with miscreations.

sources.locator: Maramoa on The Dusk and the Moon Orb

alt_summaries.summary: Sarn temple holding the Moon Orb, guarded by the exile 'Dusk'.

name: Maligaro's Sanctum
summary: A map-like area in Act 7 entered through portals opened with Maligaro's Map from the Chamber of Sins; the Artist Maligaro and his pet spider Black Death are fought here.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'You have opened the portals using his Map, now enter Maligaro's Sanctum.'
Walkthrough: 'Maligaro's Sanctum is a map-like area. Player consumes one portal to enter the area'

name: Memory Nexus
summary: Hub area of Synthesis where captured Fragmented Memories are placed to form paths to rewards, enhancements and boss memories.

alt_summaries.summary: Synthesis hub in the Atlas where stabilised memories are connected into paths to memory bosses like the Cortex.

name: Merveil's Lair
summary: Act 1 boss area at the end of the Cavern of Anger.

name: Middengard
summary: Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.

alt_summaries.summary: Distant continent east/southeast of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.
Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast, homeland of the Kalguur; ruled by a king named Cadigan; it cannot be directly visited in the games.

name: Monastery of the Keepers
summary: Southern Atlas site; hidden chamber houses the Dreamer; Genesis Tree and Grasping Orchid located here.

sources.locator: Visit the Monastery of the Keepers
hidden area in the Monastery of the Keepers
Monastery of the Keepers to grow a Grasping Orchid

alt_summaries.summary: Keepers' sanctuary housing Ailith and the Genesis Tree.
Hub reached by the Horned Skull; home of the Genesis Tree and Ailith.

name: Moti Aro
summary: Karui port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

sources.locator: Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards

name: Mount Veruso
summary: Mountain beneath which virtue gems were discovered by the Vaal, who used them to gain great power.

name: The Mud Flats (Act 6)
summary: Act 6 area reached from the Coast; its entrance is blocked by Hiveborn structures until the Into the Breach quest is started.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'approaching the entrance to the Mud Flats from the Coast in Act 6, where the entrance is blocked off by Hiveborn structures'

name: Ngakanu
summary: Tukohama-tribe settlement under Chieftain Tavakai, reached late in Act 4; a hostile Blood Fever zone after Tavakai's declaration. Kaimana lives here.

sources.locator: Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards

alt_summaries.summary: Karui port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

name: Ngamakanui
summary: Karui homeland, an archipelago southwest of Lioneye's Watch; to the Karui the name (Nga + Makanui, 'the Karui Way') denotes anywhere the Karui roam. Explorable in PoE2 Act 4, where it is overrun by the Flesh Scourge (speculative per wiki).

sources.locator: [5:33] Kahuturoa: 'Ngamakanui isn't a place, not really.'

alt_summaries.summary: Karui homeland archipelago, seat of Kaom and Hyrri; where Voll sought Kaom's help.
Karui homeland archipelago.

The Karui 'archipelago': per Kahuturoa, not a fixed place but wherever the Karui bring their Way ('Makanui is our Way'); the Karui deliberately keep its location from the Vaal. Act 4 is set among its islands around Kingsmarch.
Karui archipelago where the weapon pieces lie.

name: Oriath
summary: Island off the south-east of Wraeclast, founded by Innocence's banished followers and ruled by the Templar theocracy from Theopolis. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it served as the Empire's successor; destroyed in the Atlas storyline of PoE1 and revisited in PoE2 Act 4.

alt_summaries.summary: A small island off Wraeclast's south-east coast, founded by followers of Innocence. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it became the successor of the Eternal Empire and a Templar theocracy.
Island Theocracy ruled by the Templar.
Capital of the Templar Theocracy; fallen to Kitava's cultists, revisited in Act 10 and rebuilt in the Epilogue.

Former Templar capital destroyed by Sirus in PoE1; PoE2 outsiders think it was abandoned 20 years ago, but the Twilight Order secretly rebuilt its heart and keeps the Beast here (Kanu, Act 4). Setting of the unreleased Act 5.

name: Oriath Docks
summary: Act 10 town where Lani, Weylam and Lilly Roth, Divinia and Sin base themselves.

name: Oriath Square
summary: Square leading to the Templar Courts, Ossuary and Reliquary.

name: Overseer's Tower
summary: Act 5 town, rebel camp.

name: The Pale Court
summary: Prophecy-system area where the Pale Council bosses (Eber, Inya, Yriel, Volkuur) are fought; the wiki states this content was removed in 3.17.0.

sources.locator: Infobox location = [[The Pale Court]]; header 'The prophecy system was removed from the game in version 3.17.0'

name: Phaaryl
summary: Unexplorable location north of Sarn, said to be the point of invasion of the Harbingers as described in Commander Kirac's 'Kirac's Memory' quest dialogue. More than three thousand Oriathan soldiers were killed in the Battle of Phaaryl.

sources.locator: lead paragraph: 'an unexplorable location north of Sarn ... the point of invasion by the Harbingers, as described by Commander Kirac's Kirac's Memory quest dialogue. Over three thousand Oriathan soldiers were killed in the Battle of Phaaryl'

name: Phrecia (imperial heartlands)
summary: Imperial heartlands of the Eternal Empire named in honour of General Alano Phrecia after he drove away a pervasive darkness; contains Phrecia Cathedral (modern Fellshrine Ruins).

name: Phrecia Cathedral
summary: Cathedral seat of Archbishop Geofri in the Phrecian heartlands (today the Fellshrine Ruins); Geofri was killed here by Maligaro.

name: Pondium
summary: Kalguuran port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

sources.locator: Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards

name: Pondium (Valerie's home port)
summary: Lawless port where Valerie and Vesper grew up; Valerie says it holds more fairness than Oriath.

name: Precursor Shrine
summary: Underground shrine built around a mirror by the 'oldest of men' (probably primeval/precursor); Uhtred hid here and the Kalguuran survivors tried to reach it. No link to Kalandra's mirror is proven.

name: Prisoner's Gate (Act 6)
summary: Act 6 area with the side area Valley of the Fire Drinker where Abberath is found.

sources.locator: Located in The Valley of the Fire Drinker, side area of Prisoner's Gate

name: Riben Fell
summary: Kalguuran port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

sources.locator: Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards

name: The Rogue Harbour
summary: Hub town of the criminal guild known as the Ring, reached by a Rogue's Marker portal (introduced by an Act 6 quest from 3.13.0); home of the fence Faustus, administrator Kurai, rogues and the Wayfinder Adiyah who opens contract portals.

name: Sarn
summary: Capital of the Eternal Empire, founded by Veruso on the site of Azala Vaal. Burned during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons, rebuilt, besieged by Voll in 1334 IC and fallen within an hour of the Cataclysm. The Act 8 city of the exile.

alt_summaries.summary: Ruined Eternal Empire capital.
Eternal Empire capital founded on the ruins of Azala Vaal.

name: The Sarn Encampment
summary: Act 8 town amid the ruins of Sarn; home of Hargan, Clarissa and Maramoa.

alt_summaries.summary: Act 3 town in Sarn.

name: Sceptre of God
summary: Imperial palace tower of Sarn where Chitus, Malachai and Dialla held court (concubines kept there); the exile kills Dominus atop it in Act 3.

alt_summaries.summary: Tower in Sarn where Dominus's laboratory stands at the summit.

name: The Shaper's Realm
summary: Realm at the centre of the Atlas where the Shaper is fought ('the Crucible' in the legacy quest); the Uber Elder fight takes place in its version of the Absence of Value and Meaning.

sources.locator: Assignment 11: 'found the Shaper in the Crucible'

name: The Slave Pens
summary: Arrival area in Oriath ruled by Overseer Krow.

name: Solaris Temple
summary: Sarn temple where Malachai built the Rapture Device over more than a year; the exile meets Dialla on Level 2 in Act 3.

sources.locator: Maramoa on The Dawn and the Sun Orb

alt_summaries.summary: Temple in north-east Sarn where Lady Dialla is found.
Sarn temple holding the Sun Orb, guarded by the exile 'Dawn'.

name: Starfall Crater
summary: Area reached through an entrance that can randomly appear in ore-deposit maps; holds The Black Knight, who guards several Verisium Outcrops (Kingsmarch wiki, Bosses section).

sources.locator: ==Bosses== ===The Black Knight===: "Map areas containing ore deposits can randomly contain an entrance to the Starfall Crater, which holds the Black Knight inside guarding several Verisium Outcrops."

name: Stridevolf
summary: Enclave on the southern outskirts of the Vastiri Plains, past Mount Vastiri. It was burned down by the unnamed 'bandit king of Stridevolf' during a conflict with the Maraketh warrior Orbala. Governor Kastov is listed among its notable members.

sources.locator: lead paragraph: 'an enclave on the southern outskirts of the Vastiri Plains, past Mount Vastiri ... burned down by the bandit king of Stridevolf during a conflict with Maraketh warrior Orbala'; 'Notable members: Governor Kastov'. No date is given on the page, so era is unknown.

name: The Submerged Passage
summary: Flooded tidal cave in the Act 1 Mud Flats, behind the glyph wall. It is drained when the three Karui glyphs are fitted into the wall.

sources.locator: Quest objective 'open the Submerged Passage'; 'The Submerged Passage is now open'

name: Sulphur Vents (Delve)
summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) with Fractured, Metallic, Perfect, Aetheric and Encrusted fossils; its biome-specific nodes include Humid Fissure and Restless Rubble. Introduced in 3.4.0.

sources.locator: Intro: 'Sulfur Vents is one of the biomes of the Azurite Mine'; Fossils list; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game'

name: Tane's Laboratory
summary: Underground laboratory of Tane Octavius near the Karui Shores, undamaged by Oriath's destruction; where Metamorph work is done.

name: Te Onui
summary: Karui port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

sources.locator: Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards

name: The Templar Courts
summary: Templar stronghold built by Avarius's command; becomes Torched Courts.

name: Temple of Chaos
summary: Vaal temple near the outskirts of Utzaal where commoners could attempt the Trials of Chaos to become high priests; in PoE2 Act 3, off the Chimeral Wetlands.

sources.locator: paragraph on the Temple of Chaos

alt_summaries.summary: Temple of Vaal priests dedicated to Chaos on the outskirts of Utzaal; site of the PoE2 Trial of Chaos.

name: The Temple of Decay
summary: Arakaali's temple in the Vaal City where Silk is lost and Arakaali is killed.

sources.locator: Kill Arakaali at the heart of the Temple of Decay

alt_summaries.summary: Arakaali's temple, Act 7.

name: The Abyss (place)
summary: Underground realm reached through Abyss pits; Abyssal Depths.

name: The Aqueduct
summary: Act 4 area on the way to Highgate, where Lady Dialla first waits for the Exile to ask them to destroy the Beast.

sources.locator: Walkthrough quest log: 'Dialla is waiting for you on the Aqueduct'

name: The Ascent
summary: Mt. Veruso path east of Highgate (an Act 4 area, level 40) leading to the Resonator whose portal opens to Oriath.

name: The Bath House
summary: Sarn area where Hector Titucius guards the Wings of Vastiri.

name: The Battlefront
summary: Sarn battlefront held by the Ebony Legion. A Blackguard chest here holds the Ribbon Spool, guarded by an optional boss.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'Find the Ribbon Spool in the Battlefront'

name: The Beachhead
summary: The Beachhead is a map (several variants, e.g. Red tier and Infused) that holds the Harbinger Portal; defeating the final King Harbinger in any variant drops the unique Harbinger item pieces.

sources.locator: 'Unique pieces' and 'Harbinger scroll' sections; src_poewiki_harbinger_league 'Unique items' section

name: The Belly of the Beast / Rotting Core (Act 9)
summary: Interior of the Beast's corpse; the Black Core / Rotting Core is where the Depraved Trinity is fought.

name: The Breach (realm)
summary: Parallel realm opened by breaches in which Breachlords hold domains; see concept_breach.

sources.locator: lead: breaches open a parallel realm containing otherworldly monsters

name: The Bridge Encampment
summary: Act 7 town on the broken bridge once ruled by Kraityn, now home to Yeena, Helena, Eramir and Weylam Roth's ghost.

name: The Canals
summary: The Act 10 waterways of Oriath, behind Kitava's Horns, where Kitava feeds; Innocence opens the way to them and the Feeding Trough lies there.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'Kitava, the Insatiable's Horns block the way to the The Canals where Kitava, the Insatiable feeds.'

name: The Crematorium
summary: Slum area where Piety tortured Tolman.

name: The Desecrated Chambers
summary: Defiled Chamber of Innocence where Avarius' staff lies; Avarius, Reassembled is fought here.

name: The Dread Thicket
summary: An Act 7 area in the Northern Forest where the Fireflies needed for Yeena's Fire Dew are found.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'Search for the Firefly in the The Dread Thicket (Act 7), then deliver Firefly to Yeena.'
Progression table: 'The Dread Thicket (Act 7) 53' branching from The Northern Forest (Act 7)

name: The Dried Lake
summary: Place where Voll fled after the Cataclysm and wrote his Confession; he and his undead legion remained there for centuries.

name: The Feeding Trough
summary: Final area of Act 10 where Kitava feeds and is slain.

sources.locator: You have found Kitava at his Feeding Trough

name: The Grain Gate
summary: Sarn gate attacked by the Purity forces; failed assault repelled by Chitus' gemlings. Gemlings survive there in Act 8.

name: The Grand Arena
summary: Daresso's Dream arena modelled on Theopolis's Grand Arena.

name: The Harbour Bridge
summary: Sarn bridge with the Sky Shrine where Solaris and Lunaris are summoned and killed.

sources.locator: Sky Shrine in the center of The Harbour Bridge

name: The Library
summary: Sarn library where Siosa dwells; Archives hide the Golden Pages.

name: The Lightless Hollow
summary: Circular arena with a central abyssal pit where Zorath lies suspended; accessible directly on the Atlas.

sources.locator: Entry: "Zorath's arena is called The Lightless Hollow, and can be directly traversed to on the Atlas"

name: The Menagerie
summary: Act 2 location unlocked by completing Einhar's Hunt; Einhar gives the optional Einhar's Menagerie quest here (perform beastcrafting once).

sources.locator: Rewards and 'Quest Complete - You have unlocked the Menagerie'

name: The Mines (Highgate)
summary: Mountain mines sealed by Deshret with the Beast inside.

name: The Necropolis
summary: Graveyard where haunted corpses are buried and exorcised to add crafting modifiers to the Tome of Arimor.

sources.locator: Perform the Exorcism in The Necropolis

name: The Nightmare (Scourge realm)
summary: Ruined, demon-infested alternate version of Wraeclast the exile shifts into in Scourge; monsters there become the new Beyond monsters. Not the same as the Vaal 'crimson nightmare' realm of Atziri.

name: The Oasis
summary: Hidden oasis where Shakari rebuilds her army; she is fought in the Sand Pit.

name: The Ossuary (Act 10)
summary: Templar bone-vault in Oriath holding Atziri's Elixir of Allure (love potion in her lover's skull) and the Mortinomicon Exitio Immortalis.

alt_summaries.summary: Oriath ossuary where the Sign of Purity is found.

name: The Quarry
summary: Act 9 area with a side area for Garukhan and the blood pools around the Lesion where Sin burns a way into the Beast.

name: The Quay
summary: Sarn dockside where Clarissa's failed resurrection of Tolman takes place.

name: The Ravaged Square
summary: Oriath's square where Kitava's Horns block the way to the Canals.

sources.locator: Horns in the Ravaged Oriath Square

name: The Reliquary
summary: Holds Kitava's Torments.

name: The Sacred Grove
summary: Ancient garden carved from the land (possibly by ancestral Azmeri, 'older than the Eternal Empire') where Oshabi plants seeds; restored her connection to the land.

name: The Sewers
summary: Filthy tunnels under the river between Sarn's districts, filled with the Undying. An Undying Blockade bars the way and is burned away with Infernal Talc.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'Approach the Undying Blockade in The Sewers'

name: The Ship Graveyard
summary: Coastal wreck field where Fairgraves is marooned.

name: The Simulacrum
summary: The Simulacrum: a wave-based Delirium encounter opened by the Simulacrum map fragment in a Map Device; the fragment is crafted from Simulacrum Splinters dropped by Delirium monsters.

name: The Temple of Atzoatl
summary: Vaal temple-complex built in the last years of Atziri's reign, centre of trade, mechanical research, Chayula worship and Doryani's gem experiments; Atziri moved her seat here. PoE1 Incursion league lets players reach it 2,000 years in the past.

name: The Vaal City
summary: Vaal city risen from the depths in Act 7, accessed via the Causeway; contains Arakaali's Temple of Decay.

sources.locator: Yeena in The Vaal City near Arakaali's temple
city has risen from the depths

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal city that rose to prominence under Queen Tetzlapokal; PoE1 Act 7 area.

name: The Weaver's Chambers
summary: Spider-infested caves entered from the Western Forest.

name: The Wetlands (Act 2)
summary: Act 2 wetland area where the great tree Lorrata has rooted itself across the entrance to the Vaal Ruins. The Exile poisons the tree with Maligaro's Spike and the Baleful Gem.

sources.locator: Quest objective 'Poison the tree, Lorrata, in The Wetlands'

name: The Wetlands (Act 6)
summary: Act 6 area whose side area The Spawning Ground holds Ryslatha.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: Spawning Grounds in The Wetlands

name: Theopolis
summary: Capital city of the Theocracy of Oriath; site of the Oriath academy where Valdo worked and of the Templar Laboratory.

sources.locator: Memory of Wonder: 'a map of Theopolis'

alt_summaries.summary: Capital of Oriath and seat of the High Templar; home of the Grand Arena where Daresso fought.

name: Throne of Atziri
summary: Tier-3 incursion room of Xipocado in the Temple of Atzoatl containing a boss encounter with Atziri.

name: Trarthus
summary: Region southwest of Wraeclast and west of the Karui archipelago; capital Korathin; a brutal slave-and-killer culture ruled by four Great Houses, once the Eternal Empire's dumping ground for exiles.

alt_summaries.summary: Land south-west of Wraeclast used by the Empire as an exile colony; rebelled in 870 IC.

name: Tsoatha
summary: Ancient sunken city, domain of the Brine King; Lilly Roth wants to plunder it after his death.

sources.locator: Lilly: 'his sunken domain, the ancient city of Tsoatha'

name: The Twilight Strand
summary: The shore where each PoE1 league's Exile washes up after the Oriathan sentence, face-down in the sand.

sources.locator: section 'The Present' and 'The Atlas of Worlds'

alt_summaries.summary: Beach where exiles first wash ashore; ends at Lioneye's Watch.

name: Utzaal
summary: Vaal city, centre of Doryani's research, drowned by its own waterways at the Cataclysm to spite looters. PoE2 Act 3 setting: the Exile drains the Sunken City, then travels to its living past.

sources.locator: Quest logs 'Speak to the Hooded One' / 'Enter Utzaal in the past'
