alt_summaries.summary: Sunken Vaal city in the jungles of Act 3; the Hooded One sends the Exile to Utzaal to seek knowledge of the Beast. Its past version is reached through a time gateway.

name: The Vaal Ruins (PoE1 Act 2)
summary: Vaal ruin from which the Exile unleashes Darkness.

name: Vaal Temple (map)
summary: Atlas map area themed on Vaal corruption, containing ten Vaal Vessel strongboxes and the demon boss trio; tileset similar to the Apex of Sacrifice.

name: Vastiri (Plains / Desert)
summary: Region bordering Phaaryl, Lira Vaal and Sarn, home of the Maraketh; once a lush land of forests and seven rivers around Keth, it became a desert over thousands of years after the Beast silenced the gods.

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh desert east of Highgate with the oasis shielded by Shakari's sandstorm.

name: The Well of Souls
summary: Wellspring of necromancy that collects all souls; Kulemak's seat. In PoE2 reached via the Lightless Passage from Mastodon Badlands in Act 2; later the Abyss hub.

alt_summaries.summary: Source of necromantic power that collects all souls; hub area in PoE2 Abyss content.

name: Wraeclast
summary: The continent on which the Exile's story takes place; PoE2 is set on (and expands) Wraeclast, while Oriath is another continent seen in PoE1.

alt_summaries.summary: The continent where the Exile is sent. It was the site of the Precursor, Primeval, Vaal and Eternal Empire civilisations, and the Cataclysm's effects were mostly confined to its landmass.
Forsaken continent where exiles are sent.
Continent of the Path of Exile setting.

name: Aberrations
summary: Environmental lore objects tied to the Originator (Zana) and her father Valdo. Most entries are narrated by Zana: the Atlas as a trap, Sirus's transformation by the Atlas, her intervention through memory threads to save him, and the Templars' brutality. The entries in the Incarnation boss arenas are narrated by Valdo.

sources.locator: lead: 'environmental lore objects found in areas related to Zana, the Originator ... the ones in the Incarnation boss arenas are narrated by Valdo'; 'Entry 2 (The Success)': 'I set the threads in motion across time and space'; 'The Neglected Flame' on Sirus

name: Al-Hezmin's Journals
summary: Four clickable hunter's journals from Al-Hezmin's arena. They are notes on his companions (Baran's prayers, Veritania's reading, Zana's secrets, Drox's drills), his rivalry with Drox, and a final entry about a 'New Person' who talked with Zana and seemed stronger than the other exiles.

sources.locator: section 'Journal I' (Baran: 'Prayer is the centre of his regimen'; Zana: 'Hiding something important') to 'Journal IV': 'New Person: I don't recognise this one ... Saw them talking to Zana.'

name: Ancient Etchings (Kalandra)
summary: Series of Ancient Etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra herself, recounting her entrapment, scorn for gods (Etching V: a conversation with someone implied to be Sin), and the Order of the Djinn's failed rescue (Etching VI).

sources.locator: Prehistory > The Lake of Kalandra footnotes
Ancient Etchings entry (found throughout the Lake)

alt_summaries.summary: Series of etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra: her entry, view of gods as 'thieves of virtue', a conversation with a 'little thief' (Sin), the Order of the Djinn's abandoned promise, and a new escape plan.

name: Baran's Journals
summary: Four clickable journals from Baran's arena: a will bequeathing his staff and platemail to Veritania, Sirus, Drox and Al-Hezmin and his Oriathan home to Templar siblings; a letter to Landren about being trapped in the Atlas; a letter to a discoverer describing the demon that fed on Valdo Caeserius's memories ('the Decay') and Sirus's sacrifice; and a final entry in which Baran turns to God and plans to take the Atlas.

sources.locator: section 'Journal I' (Last Will and Testament: 'To my good friends and allies, Veritania, Sirus, Drox, and Al-Hezmin'), 'Journal III' ('feeding on the memories of Valdo Caeserius'), 'Journal IV' ('I am your sword')

name: Journals of the Conquerors
summary: Lore objects in the Conquerors' arenas (added 3.9.2) narrating each Elderslayer's descent.

name: Drox's Journals
summary: Four clickable journals in Drox's arena in which the former exile pursues a kingdom of law and justice through force, conquers valley after valley and grows more convinced that strength will make the mists real, ending as 'Drox the Warlord'.

sources.locator: section 'Journal I' ('Drox the Just') to 'Journal IV' ('Drox the Warlord.'); Journal I: 'I shall be the one who leads')

name: Feverish Writings (Niko)
summary: Letter by Niko ('Your master, Niko') in the Doomed Mine on the Isle of Kin, urging miners to gather sulphite while a blind beast whispers in the dark. Continues PoE1's Niko (Delve) into PoE2.

name: Letter (Kingsmarch environmental lore)
summary: Rotating letters in the Kingsmarch tavern by Johan, Raulf, Sonja, Dannig, Rog, Tujen, Gwennen, Faustus and Isla revealing their secret rebel ties, loves and loyalties.

name: Letters from Chitus
summary: Three letters from Chitus to Cadiro (1316-1318 IC) planning to win Izaro's Labyrinth. Released as physical GGG merchandise.

name: Letters of Exile
summary: Environmental lore object in Lioneye's Watch: court papers nailed to stakes that give the sentences of named exiles (1597-1599 IC) in the formula 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. Added in version 0.10.8. Distinct from text_letters_from_chitus (Chitus's letters to Cadiro) and text_vaal_letters (Vaal victims' letters).

sources.locator: intro: 'Letters of Exile is an environmental lore object found in Lioneye's Watch.'; section '==Format==' sentencing formula; version history 0.10.8

name: Lifegiver's Manifesto
summary: Catarina's writings in Syndicate hideouts urging an immortal new world order and herself as eternal queen.

name: The Lord's Labyrinth (gamebook)
summary: An official GGG gamebook (2019) that retells the Lord's Labyrinth from Weylin's perspective. The PoE Wiki reports repeated inconsistencies with in-game sources, so it is generally not treated as canon.

sources.locator: gamebook forum post, 28 Oct 2019 (cited in History of Wraeclast, 'The Lord's Labyrinth')
section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' (gamebook note: generally not canon)

name: Lycia's relics
summary: Forbidden Sanctum relics revealing the Original Sin and Innocence's ascension.

name: Path of Exile: Origins
summary: Official comic recounting Victario, the Karui Way, the Chamber of Sins and Chitus' death.

name: Path of Exile: Origins (comic)
summary: A four-issue official comic by Grinding Gear Games and Dynamite Entertainment, told from Victario's perspective. Digital issues ran from July 2014 to April 2015; the paperback was published by Dynamite in June 2015. It centres on the Purity Rebellion and events leading up to the Cataclysm.

sources.locator: 'Publication' section (issue table) and intro: written by Edwin McRae and Royal McGraw, illustrated by Carlos Rodriguez

name: The Purity Chronicles
summary: Six-book chronicle by Garivaldi in the Library of Sarn (Act 3 area) on the Purity Rebellion.

name: Memory Fragments of the Shaper
summary: Seven in-game diary entries (Home, Intrigue, Wonder, Dream, Nightmare, Grief, Awakening) in which Valdo describes the golden device, dreams, Zana's capture and resolving to 'forge a world anew'. Partly superseded by the Book of Memories retcon.

name: Sirus' Journals
summary: Four clickable lore journals in the Conquerors of the Atlas boss rooms that expand the story of Sirus, Awakener of Worlds: his wish for purpose, his dread of the monster the group pursues, the last days with his companions, and his entrapment and 'empty' existence after he stepped into an orb of darkness.

sources.locator: section 'Journal 1' ('If it weren't for Zana...') to 'Journal 4' ('They left me. In my moment of need, they left me.' ... 'Empty.')

name: Chamber of Innocence stained glass windows
summary: Templar propaganda in Oriath depicting Innocence as pure and Sin as deceitful twin; later contradicted by Lycia.

name: The Ancients (Trinian)
summary: In-game history by Trinian in the Library of Sarn (PoE1 Act 3), Books 1-5 on Atziri, Zerphi, Doryani, the Azmeri and the Fall.

name: Vaal Letters
summary: Twelve readable letters by victims and subjects of Atziri's regime, documenting sacrifice and dissent.

name: Veritania's Journals
summary: Four clickable journal entries that appeared in Veritania's arena after she was defeated. They trace her from a self-described disciplined exile who is disgusted by Atlas vice, to the self-appointed 'Redeemer' who plans to purge the mortals who indulge.

sources.locator: section 'Journal I' to 'Journal IV': e.g. Journal III 'I am the only one that can save us', signed 'Veritania the Pure'; Journal IV 'I shall save you from your own vices by purging your weakness.' signed 'Veritania the Redeemer'

name: Victario's Writings
summary: Four environmental lore texts in The Library, written as anecdotes and allegory by the poet Victario of Sarn: Kalisa Maas and the Virtue gem that shatters glass; the Blackest Monkey parable; Slaves of Virtue, on shackled workers who mine gems for the Eternal citizens while Malachai abuses them; and A Friend in Need, on the musician Lorenzi who has a gem implanted in his hand.

sources.locator: section headings 'Volume 1: Kalisa Maas', 'Volume 2: The Blackest Monkey', 'Volume 3: Slaves of Virtue' (mentions Malachai and Highgate), 'Volume 4: A Friend in Need' (Lorenzi and Malachai's gem implant); each signed 'Victario of Sarn'

name: Voll's Confession
summary: Voll's confession that he trusted the most corrupt of men.

name: The Word of the Dreamer
summary: Environmental-lore book in the Monastery of the Keepers written by Ailith recording five visions of the Dreamer. Four visions warn of the Mother (births flesh), the Red Pyre (flame/addiction), the Forked Psyche (thought without will) and the Preserved Patterns (imprisoned bodies), each of whom the Dreamer 'once knew'; the fifth says the Four have become One and that the Genesis Tree is his gift. The mapping of these four to Uul-Netol (flesh), Xoph (fire), Esh (forked thought) and Tul (preserved/frozen) is inference from epithets and the wiki's note that the book is about the four Breachlords that became Xesht.
